`PermissionedDomains` and `SingleAssetVault` were observed `ENABLED` on Devnet
at ~~**2026-08-24T14:42:31Z**~~ **2026-08-28T04:45:40.875Z**, alongside
`MPTokensV1`, `DynamicMPT` and `LendingProtocol`. **That reading expires.**
Re-check before relying on it.
(`SingleAssetVault` is required to *write* `sfDomainID` even though no `Vault`
object is ever created.)

⚠ **Everything here runs on Devnet with throwaway keys.** Nothing in this
project is secure, audited, non-custodial or production-ready, and nothing
should ever hold value.

## 7. Two designs that were considered and rejected

**Building on XLS-66, the lending protocol.** Rejected. Five independent
blockers, any one sufficient: a vault share token cannot be made confidential;
vault and broker pseudo-accounts can neither convert into nor receive a
confidential balance, because they cannot sign; every loan and vault value is a
plaintext ledger field; there are no revolving drawdowns, only discrete public
`Loan` objects; and value must leave confidentiality before it can enter a vault
at all. Evidenced on Devnet, not read from a specification.

**A hybrid — an XLS-65 `Vault` for the funding side, confidential transfers for
drawdowns.** Rejected, and the reason is worth stating because it is not the
obvious one. **A `Vault`'s share token cannot be confidential**, so the hybrid
forces a hard choice: *native share accounting* **or** *confidential investor
positions*, never both. The accounting is arithmetic an application can do; the
confidential position is the thing that does not exist elsewhere. And since
`TransferFee` is forced to zero and interest settles off-ledger anyway, the
share-price arithmetic was never going on-chain to begin with.

**A consequence worth noticing:** because every participant is a confidential
holder in one issuance, **the number of funders stops mattering to the
architecture.** One bank or twenty investors — the design does not fork.

Both rejections are recorded, with their evidence and their reversal conditions,
in `docs/decisions/ADR-0002-facility-as-application-logic.md`.

## 8. Where the claims in this document come from

Every capability statement above traces to `CLAIMS.md`, which grades each claim
by whether it was **executed**, **read at source**, or **inferred** — and which
carries a list of things this project may never claim. If a sentence here reads
as stronger than the register, the register wins and the sentence is a defect.

**Reusing this material:** the §5 disclosures are not optional context. A
version of this that keeps the walkthrough and drops "identities and timing are
public, the issuer decrypts everything, and the frequency leak is real and
unmitigated" is not a shorter explainer. It is a claim this project has spent
its whole life refusing to make.

*Open:* `kOversizeMetaDataCap = 5200`. Confidential state updates write ciphertexts into metadata for both parties plus mirrors. Whether that approaches the cap has not been checked. Check it before asserting anything about ledger impact.

**Fee. Grade A.** `Protocol.h:492` — `kConfidentialFeeMultiplier = 9`, passed by `ConfidentialMPTSend::calculateBaseFee`. RippleX docs independently give **100 drops** before load scaling for a single-signed confidential transaction, against 10 for a standard one; multi-signed is `10 × (10 + signatures)`. *The exact arithmetic relating the constant to the result was not verified — `Transactor::calculateBaseFee` was not read. Two sources agree on 100 drops; the mechanism is stated as inference.*

Fee escalation multiplies that base as it does any transaction. **The 10× fee floor, not byte count, is what a high-throughput confidential application budgets for.**

**Reserve. Grade A.** An `MPToken` is an owner-reserve object, and spec §7.4 adds a **deletion blocker**: once confidential fields are initialised the `MPToken` can never be deleted, *even at zero balance*. The reserve is locked for the life of the account. A holder who opts in once can never reclaim it. `MPTokenIssuance` can only be deleted when `sfConfidentialOutstandingAmount` is 0.

**Timing. ~~UNUSABLE.~~ REPLACED 2026-08-16.** Spec §14.2's ~44.8 ms / ~22.6 ms on a "laptop-class CPU" remain unusable under P-8 and are still never to be quoted. Measured replacements, full hardware and flags in `benchmarks-2026-08-16.md`: on an Apple M3 Pro under clang 21 `-O3`, aggregated Bulletproof (m=2, the Send case) proving **median 34.583 ms** and verification **median 16.100 ms** over 50 runs; the 192 B compact sigma adds **0.214 ms** proving and **0.328 ms** verification. **The sigma proofs are free and the Bulletproof is the entire cost** — the sigma component is 0.6% of proving and 2.0% of verification.

**Decryption is the cost nobody budgeted for.** It is not in §14.2 at all, and at the default window it is two orders of magnitude more expensive than proving: ~2.5 s versus ~35 ms. See §6 of the benchmarks and CLAIMS.md F-7.

---

## 7. Compliance gating — mechanism Grade A, availability folded into GAP-1

`ConfidentialMPTSend` has no `DomainID` field. Its preclaim calls `requireAuth` on **both sender and destination**, then `credentials::valid`, then `checkDepositPreauth` — explicitly *before* the expensive proof verification — and only then verifies proofs.

The domain gate lives inside `requireAuth` (`MPTokenHelpers.cpp`): it reads `sfDomainID` from the `MPTokenIssuance`, asserts `lsfMPTRequireAuth`, and calls `credentials::validDomain`. **So Permissioned Domain membership does gate confidential transfers, at the issuance level, enforced on both parties.**

**The dependency nobody would predict. Grade A.** `MPTokenIssuanceCreate.cpp:31–36`:

```cpp
if (ctx.tx.isFieldPresent(sfDomainID) &&
    !(ctx.rules.enabled(featurePermissionedDomains) &&
      ctx.rules.enabled(featureSingleAssetVault)))
```

Writing `sfDomainID` requires **`PermissionedDomains` *and* `SingleAssetVault` (XLS-65)**. Both are `Supported::Yes`, so this is not blocked on unshipped code — it is blocked on what the target network has enabled.

**W-CONF therefore needs three amendments live on the Confidential Devnet simultaneously: `ConfidentialTransfer`, `PermissionedDomains` and `SingleAssetVault`.** A devnet stood up specifically for XLS-96 may carry the first without the others. This is the most likely way the compliance third of the project dies, and `tools/check-amendments.ts` already checks all three.

**N-1. Grade A.** `MPTokenIssuanceSet.cpp:369–376` — setting `sfDomainID` to zero calls `makeFieldAbsent`. **The issuer can unilaterally remove the domain gate at any time, with no holder consent.** Belongs in the trust model alongside clawback.

---

## 8. Findings — the documentation contradicts the specification in four places, and is wrong in all four

Revised after the verification round. This is now a documentation-accuracy finding, not a claim about protocol weakness — the earlier framing risked presenting a documented design choice as a discovered flaw.

**Each of the four was checked against the rippled 3.3.0 transactors. The implementation agrees with the specification every time.**

**F-1 — The canonical encrypted zero is publicly detectable. Grade A, verified.**
Docs: the post-merge inbox value *"is indistinguishable from other ciphertexts to observers without the private key."* Spec §9.4: validators can compare against the known `EncZero` and, if they match, *"the balance is publicly known to be exactly 0."*

`encryptCanonicalZeroAmount(pubKey, account, mptIssuanceID)` is called in all three places:
- `ConfidentialMPTConvert.cpp:305–313` — first-time opt-in initialises the spending balance
- `ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox.cpp:111–114` — inbox reset after merge
- `ConfidentialMPTClawback.cpp:138–166` — spending, inbox, issuer mirror and auditor mirror

All three inputs are public. Any observer can recompute and byte-compare. **A freshly-opted-in holder's spending balance, and any holder's inbox after a merge, are publicly identifiable as exactly zero.** The documentation is wrong. Balances that reach zero by homomorphic subtraction remain opaque — that is what spec §10.7.2 describes, and the documentation generalises the wrong case.

**F-2 — "Issuer-mediated auditing" is not scoped disclosure. Grade A on the mechanism, B on the consequence.**
Spec §13.2.2 describes *"a separate set of view keys."* **No such field exists** — `MPTokenIssuance` carries exactly `sfIssuerEncryptionKey` and `sfAuditorEncryptionKey`. The docs describe the real mechanism: the issuer shares its own ElGamal private key, granting *"the same decryption capabilities as the issuer."*

Stated in two layers, per Gemini's correction:
- **Protocol capability:** issuer keys are permanent and cannot be rotated.
- **Operational consequence:** an issuer who chooses Mechanism 2 grants disclosure that can never be withdrawn, because the key can never be rotated.

The second follows from the first only once the choice is made. Prefer the on-chain auditor key.

**F-3 — Enabling confidentiality is one-way. Grade A, verified.**
Docs: *"can be toggled on and off as long as no confidential balances exist."* Spec §6.3.3: one-way, no disable flag. `MPTokenIssuanceSet.cpp` handles `tfMPTSetCanHoldConfidentialBalance` and `tifMPTCanHoldConfidentialBalance` only; there is no clear flag anywhere in its flag handling. The documentation is wrong. *(Method: absence across the transactor plus the spec's explicit statement. Weaker than a positive read — re-derive from the full flag enumeration if it matters.)*

**F-4 — Clawback increments the version counter. Grade A, verified.**
Docs: *"the version counter is reset to 0."* `ConfidentialMPTClawback.cpp:150` calls `incrementConfidentialVersion`. The documentation is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that breaks integrations: a wallet predicting a post-clawback version of 0 binds proofs to the wrong value and fails with `tecBAD_PROOF`.

**Two specification errata, separate from the above:**

**F-5 — Grade A, executed.** Spec §11.1 instructs the issuer to set a `RevealedAmount` field. `grep -i revealed sfields.macro` returns nothing. The implemented field is `sfMPTAmount`, which spec §11.2's own table names correctly. The prose is stale.

**F-6 — Grade A, verified.** Spec §11 and §11.4 say clawed-back funds are burned; the closing sentence of §11.2 says they move to the issuer's public reserve. `ConfidentialMPTClawback.cpp:170–179` decrements both `sfConfidentialOutstandingAmount` and `sfOutstandingAmount` with no credit to any account. Funds burn. The §11.2 sentence is the error.

**Publication order.** File all four documentation errors and both errata upstream first. Publish second. F-4 and F-1 have operational consequences for integrators, which is what makes them worth reporting rather than merely noting.

---

## 9. Domain recommendation — revised

The previous revision claimed the restructured facility "shows nothing about which supplier drew how much." **All three review passes independently found that false, and they were right.** Sender and receiver are public on every transfer, so an observer sees which supplier drew, when, and how often. Only the quantity is hidden. This section is rewritten.

### What the restructure actually buys

Value must enter confidentiality **once, in aggregate**, and every per-participant event must be a `ConfidentialMPTSend`:

1. The funding bank issues the MPT and creates a Dedicated Account — the issuer account is forbidden from holding confidential balances of its own issuance.
2. The bank funds the vault publicly with the whole facility float; the vault converts **once**. Public: total facility size — which investors need.

   > **Terminology hazard, flagged 2026-08-16 (ADR-0002).** "The vault" here means the **Dedicated Account** of step 1 — an ordinary XRPL account — **not** an XLS-65 `Vault` ledger object. That distinction was harmless when written and is now load-bearing: an XLS-65 `Vault` pseudo-account **cannot** convert, so reading the word as the ledger object makes this step impossible. Prefer "Dedicated Account" throughout from here on.
3. Every drawdown is a `ConfidentialMPTSend` from vault to supplier. Amount hidden.
4. Every repayment is a `ConfidentialMPTSend` back. Amount hidden.
5. `ConvertBack` only when the facility is retired or resized. Public: aggregate change.

**Precisely:** this eliminates plaintext disclosure through `Convert` events. It does not eliminate metadata leakage. Remaining public: the counterparty set, the fact and timing of every drawdown and repayment, drawdown frequency per supplier, aggregate facility size, and `ConfidentialOutstandingAmount`.

### Does the domain survive the residual leak?

The original justification was that drawdown level and financing terms reveal a supplier's cash position. Assessed against what actually leaks:

- **Drawdown level** — hidden. The justification's core holds.
- **Financing terms** — never on-ledger at all. `TransferFee` must be 0 for confidential issuances, so fees and interest are computed off-ledger regardless.
- **Cash position inferred from drawdown frequency** — **leaks.** A supplier moving from monthly to weekly draws is legible as stress without any amount being known.

**Recommendation: the domain survives, conditional on the application generating scheduled cover traffic.** *(New argument. **Still Proposed and still unreviewed as an argument.** Revised 2026-08-17 — see the corrections immediately below, which both REVIEW-004 legs forced.)*

> **CORRECTION, 2026-08-17.** This paragraph previously asserted that a zero-amount send "is indistinguishable from a non-zero send" as settled fact, and rested the whole recommendation on it. **That overstated the evidence and was the highest-severity finding of REVIEW-004** (Codex leg finding 1; Gemini HIGH-01). What is now established, and what is not:
>
> - **Validity is settled — Grade A, executed.** A zero-amount `ConfidentialMPTSend` is accepted and validated on Devnet. That is CLAIMS.md E-22(a) and it is the limb that would have killed this recommendation outright.
> - **Indistinguishability is NOT settled and cannot be settled by this method.** It survived three falsification checks under a controlled rerun — randomisation across repeats, non-match against recomputed canonical `EncZero`, and a like-for-like comparison against non-zero sends at an identical sender balance with the fee threshold measured on both arms. **Surviving three attempts to break it is not a proof.** That is E-22(b), graded C.
> - **The count itself was wrong.** An earlier write-up claimed "four checks"; the first of the four was validity, which is limb (a), so the count used one claim as evidence for a different one.
> - **What this recommendation actually needs has not been built:** an adversary model over transaction *sequences*. Every check to date compares one transaction against another. Cover traffic is a claim about traffic patterns over time — timing, counterparty graph, `sfDestinationTag`, and correlation against the issuer's plaintext `sfConfidentialOutstandingAmount`. None of that is tested.
>
> **Treat cover traffic as an unverified proposal, not a mitigation, until that model exists.** See CLAIMS.md B-10 and `REVIEW-004c-adjudication-2026-08-17.md` §2.

The protocol supports it natively as far as *validity* goes: a `ConfidentialMPTSend` of zero is a valid transaction — the aggregated Bulletproof proves the amount lies in [0, 2⁶⁴), and zero is in range — and its ciphertexts are freshly randomised rather than canonical. The canonical `EncZero` of F-1 is used only for initialisation and resets, never for send amounts.

So the *shape* of the mitigation is: the vault sends to **every** enrolled supplier on a fixed cadence, whether or not value moves. If indistinguishability holds, drawdown frequency becomes a constant and stops carrying signal. Cost is one transaction per supplier per period at **10× the network base fee** — trivial. *(Corrected 2026-08-17: this previously said "100 drops", which is the ratio against a base fee of 10. The multiplier is the durable fact and was measured on 2026-08-17; the absolute number is network-dependent — CLAIMS.md E-5.)* What still leaks is the counterparty set: who is enrolled on the facility. That is generally not secret, since a buyer's supplier list is usually discoverable, and it should be disclosed as accepted rather than defended.

If cover traffic is judged too artificial for a reference application, the honest alternative is to keep the domain and state plainly that timing is public — but then the commercial justification is weaker than the prompt claims, and that must be said in the README rather than glossed.

### The alternative that may make this moot

> **ANSWERED 2026-08-16 — it does not make it moot. See `XLS-66-INVESTIGATION-2026-08-16.md`.**
> XLS-66 models a fixed-term amortising loan with no revolving drawdowns, and **no asset inside the lending protocol can carry a confidential balance** — the vault share MPT cannot be created with the flag and cannot acquire it later, and vault and broker pseudo-accounts can neither convert into nor receive a confidential balance because they cannot sign. Separately, every loan and vault value is a plaintext ledger field. **Recommendation: build as application logic. The domain does not move.** Tested on Devnet, not only read.
> Two consequences for the rest of this section: §9's facility design stands unchanged, and the second carry-forward item below is **dissolved rather than answered** — a pseudo-account cannot hold a confidential balance, so nobody tracks one. The first carry-forward item is unchanged and still reviewed by nobody.

The reading that raised the question, retained for context:

`LendingProtocol` (XLS-66) is **enabled on standard Devnet as of 2026-08-16** — not merely `Supported::Yes` — alongside all three amendments W-CONF needs (E-26). It has native `Vault`, `LoanBroker` and `Loan` ledger objects. Before committing to application-layer facility logic, establish whether XLS-66 already models the facility natively and whether its share tokens can be confidential MPTs. If they can, the project becomes "confidential positions in a native lending vault" — sharper, and resting on two amendments instead of one. If they cannot, that incompatibility is itself a finding. **This is the highest-value hour available and it should precede the naming sweep**, since it may change the domain and therefore the name.

#### Two things above must not be inherited silently if the domain moves

*Added 2026-08-16. Both are load-bearing parts of §9 that are weaker than they look, and a change of domain is exactly the moment they get carried across without re-examination.*

1. **The cover-traffic recommendation is `Proposed` and reviewed by nobody.** It is the sole reason §9 concludes the domain survives its residual metadata leak. It also depends on **E-22, which is Grade C — inferred, not tested.** If the facility moves into a native XLS-66 vault, the counterparty and timing leaks change shape entirely: drawdowns may become `Loan` object state transitions rather than `ConfidentialMPTSend`s, and a cover-traffic scheme designed for the latter may be irrelevant, insufficient, or impossible. **Re-derive the leak analysis for the new mechanism. Do not port the conclusion.**

2. **R-5 was un-retracted on 2026-08-16** (see CLAIMS.md). The single-conversion facility design — the vault converting the whole float in one `ConfidentialMPTConvert` — **is live again**, because the 1,000,000 decryption bound turned out to be a caller-supplied search window rather than a ceiling (F-7). What replaced the float cap is a **balance-tracking requirement**: whoever holds the confidential balance must maintain its expected value off-ledger to decrypt cheaply, and resynchronisation costs ~2.49 µs per unit of uncertainty with no sublinear fallback shipped (F-8; true at mpt-crypto `1.0.4`, and upstream added one in `1.0.5`, E-297). **If a native vault pseudo-account holds the confidential balance, establish who performs that tracking and whether a pseudo-account can.** That question has no answer yet and it is not obviously favourable.

**Neither of these blocks the XLS-66 investigation. Both block accepting its recommendation.**

### Constraints to design around

- **`TransferFee` must be 0.** Fees and interest settle off-ledger or as separate confidential sends.
- **Clawback burns the holder's entire balance** and cannot model partial recovery. It is a sanctions instrument, not a repayment mechanism.

### Why not the confidential fund share register

Same plaintext-conversion problem at subscription and redemption, no secondary market (XLS-96 forbids DEX integration; XLS-82 is `Supported::No`), and it is the example Ripple's own material uses.

## 10. If ConfidentialTransfer never activates on mainnet

Nothing about the build changes — devnet-only is a project rule, not a consequence of amendment status. The README changes: it must then say the artifact exercises a feature that **is not enabled on Mainnet and may never be**, with dated `feature` RPC output pasted in.

The opposite failure is likelier to bite. If the amendment activates mid-build, every "not enabled" statement in the repository becomes false, and a stale README is a correctness bug in our own writing. Date every status claim; re-run the checker before each publication.

This could be the whole project. /**
 * Known Devnet accounts, so the demonstration does not open on an empty form.
 *
 * ⚠⚠ **PUBLIC LEDGER DATA ONLY, AND THE OMISSION IS DELIBERATE.** An account
 * address and an `MPTokenIssuanceID` are readable by anyone with a block
 * explorer — that is `CLAIMS.md` P-4 and P-11, and rendering them gives nothing
 * away that the protocol was hiding.
 *
 * ⚠ **`/tmp/wconf/state.json` IS NOT READ AND MUST NOT BE.** That file holds
 * throwaway account seeds and ElGamal secrets. The addresses below were
 * transcribed from it by hand, once, and **the secrets stayed there** — a
 * read-only rendering tier that opens a file full of seed material has become
 * something else, whatever it does with the contents. If this list needs to
 * grow, transcribe the public fields again rather than teaching this process to
 * read that file.
 *
 * ⚠ **It is a convenience, not a registry.** The observer and issuer views take
 * any account and issuance; this only saves pasting 34 and 48 characters.
 */

export interface DemoAccount {
  address: string;
  issuanceId: string;
  label: string;
  /** What this account is useful for showing. Rendered, so it is a claim. */
  note: string;
}

/** The issuance every account below holds. */
export const DEMO_ISSUANCE = "004625C9F2DDC3E652071A9FFA07507F2151FEE332CB25E8";

export const DEMO_ACCOUNTS: DemoAccount[] = [
  {
    address: "rHeah37pL6aFPf59nzWGwujPzSFkp4TUL8",
    issuanceId: DEMO_ISSUANCE,
    label: "Holder A — an active position",
    // ⚠ This note described the account's balances, which are a ledger reading
    // and change whenever anyone sends to it; the page prints the reading
    // beside it (`REVIEW-059` R1-14). Notes describe the account, never its state.
    note: "One of the two accounts the observer view was first read against, on 2026-08-28 (CLAIMS.md E-208).",
  },
  {
    address: "rDYMkRMh7o7QfkNaoGvtd7TgFzmt12FEM8",
    issuanceId: DEMO_ISSUANCE,
    label: "Holder B — a derived-key account",
    note:
      "Onboarded with the derived key, so its ElGamal key comes from its master seed.",
  },
  {
    address: "rsc9Z29Qz6w99TnpECxbeU6vBs2L3E3CbY",
    issuanceId: DEMO_ISSUANCE,
    label: "Holder C — the ed25519 signing account",
    note:
      "The account the hedged ed25519 signing ran on. Its ledger view is ordinary: an observer " +
      "cannot see the signing change.",
  },
  {
    address: "rEVXh6wpmhKvuot95mNMb4DmkJsZqkdsWH",
    issuanceId: DEMO_ISSUANCE,
    label: "Holder D — an early spike account",
    note: "An early test account, kept as a second position to compare against.",
  },
];

/**
 * ⚠ **Every entry is checked to be a plausible address and issuance id before
 * it is served**, because a typo here renders as "this account holds nothing"
 * — which reads exactly like a true statement about the ledger.
 */
export function validDemoAccounts(): DemoAccount[] {
  return DEMO_ACCOUNTS.filter(
    (a) => /^r[1-9A-HJ-NP-Za-km-z]{24,34}$/.test(a.address) && /^[0-9A-F]{48}$/.test(a.issuanceId),
  );
}
/**
 * What a full-ledger observer sees of one position.
 *
 * ⚠ Rendered by the local tier's observer route and by the hosted build's,
 * so the observer text has one body (`ADR-0004`). `data-ledger-value` marks
 * each ledger datum, which is how the hosted gate finds the pages that must
 * carry the risk wording.
 *
 * `lists={false}` leaves out what is public and what is hidden, for a page
 * that shows several positions and renders `ObserverLists` once above them.
 */
import { Panel } from "../components/Verdict";

export function ObserverReading({ view, lists = true }: { view: any; lists?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Panel title="What a full-ledger observer sees">
        <div className="text-sm space-y-1 mb-4">
          <div><span className="opacity-60">public MPT balance</span> <code data-ledger-value="">{view.publicAmount}</code></div>
          <div><span className="opacity-60">registered</span> <code data-ledger-value="">{String(view.registered)}</code></div>
          <div><span className="opacity-60">ConfidentialBalanceVersion</span> <code data-ledger-value="">{view.confidentialBalanceVersion}</code></div>
          <div><span className="opacity-60">ConfidentialOutstandingAmount</span> <code data-ledger-value="">{view.issuance.confidentialOutstandingAmount}</code> (public: the total of all confidential balances)</div>
        </div>
        {["spending", "inbox"].map((k) => {
          const ct = (view as any)[k];
          if (!ct) return <p key={k} className="text-sm opacity-60">no {k} ciphertext</p>;
          return (
            <div key={k} className={`mt-3 p-3 rounded border ${ct.publiclyKnownZero ? "border-[var(--color-warn)]" : "border-black/10 dark:border-white/15"}`}>
              <div className="text-xs font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide opacity-60">{k}</div>
              <code className="text-[10px] break-all block my-1 opacity-80" data-ledger-value="">{ct.ciphertext}</code>
              <p className="text-sm">{ct.note}</p>
            </div>
          );
        })}
      </Panel>

      {lists && <ObserverLists view={view} />}
    </>
  );
}

/** What is public and what is hidden, the same for every position. */
export function ObserverLists({ view }: { view: any }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Panel title="Public">
        <ul className="text-sm space-y-1 list-disc pl-5">
          {view.whatIsPublic.map((s: string) => <li key={s}>{s}</li>)}
        </ul>
      </Panel>

      <Panel title="Hidden">
        <ul className="text-sm space-y-1 list-disc pl-5">
          {view.whatIsHidden.map((s: string) => <li key={s}>{s}</li>)}
        </ul>
      </Panel>
    </>
  );
}

Read in full — Dore & Cenk, RippleX Research, 2026-05-12. **ADR-0001's central premise is confirmed:** `sk_A` is a witness component of the send relation, balance linkage is proved as `B₂ − b·G = sk_A·B₁` precisely because `r_b` is unavailable to the prover, and 2-special soundness extracts `sk_A`. B-7 resolved → E-33. See `GAP-3-compact-sigma-2026-08-16.md`.

**Two things came out of it that were not being looked for.** (1) **E-4 regraded A → B**: the paper totals a Send at **1177 B**, not 1276, because it treats `C₁` as shared across all four ciphertexts and transmitted once on-chain. 99 bytes, unresolved, decidable by one devnet transaction. (2) **E-34, nonce reuse leaks `sk_A` and is undetectable from the proofs** — the sharpest cryptographic constraint yet found on ADR-0001's local-proving decision.

**With GAP-1, GAP-3 and GAP-6 closed, the remaining architecture blockers are the domain question (§9) and ADR-0001's second review round.** GAP-2 is W-PQ's, not W-CONF's.

**GAP-11 — is `mpt-crypto-sys` published on crates.io? ~~NOT ESTABLISHED.~~ CLOSED 2026-08-17, same day.**
**Yes, and so is a safe wrapper.** `mpt-crypto-sys` (FFI) and `mpt-crypto` (safe Rust wrappers) are both on crates.io at `0.1.0-beta.1`, published 2026-06-08 from **`XRPLF/xrpl-rust`**. See CLAIMS.md E-57. **The original refusal was a missing User-Agent on our side, not a crates.io policy** — the gap was correctly recorded rather than backfilled, and it closed on a proper retry. **Consequence for ADR-0001: the Rust signer's FFI substrate is not work this project has to do.** The open question is version drift — both crates are `beta.1`, unrepublished since 2026-06-08, while the C library moved `0.4.0-rc4` → `1.0.4` → `85dbac7` over the same period. Check the pin before scoping. Original text follows.

~~Opened 2026-08-17. mpt-crypto builds a self-contained static archive explicitly for a Rust crate of that name and for xrpl-py's CFFI binding (CLAIMS.md E-54), so the FFI substrate for ADR-0001's Rust signer is being built upstream. Whether the crate itself is published could not be determined: `crates.io/api/v1/crates/mpt-crypto-sys` refused with a data-access policy error. **No substitute source was used and no inference was drawn.** This is a five-minute check that materially changes the Rust signer estimate — do it before scoping that work. **GAP-6 — mpt-crypto header constants. ~~UNREAD.~~ CLOSED 2026-08-16.**
Repo cloned, `include/` read at `0.4.0-rc4` and `1.0.4`, library built, tests run. **Every constant matches the specification exactly** — 192, 754, 688, 128, 64, 66, 33 — and the two Bulletproof sizes are confirmed by *execution*, not just by reading: `test_bulletproof_agg` prints 688 B for m=1 and 754 B for m=2. §3 and §6 regrade B → A. ## 3. Transaction set — Grade A

From `transactions.macro` and `sfields.macro` at 3.3.0, cross-checked against the spec. Type numbers match exactly.

| Tx | Type | Delegable | ZKProof | Proof obligation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ConfidentialMPTConvert` | 85 | **No** | 64 B, optional | Schnorr PoK, only when registering the holder key. Otherwise the disclosed `BlindingFactor` lets validators verify deterministically with no ZKP. |
| `ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox` | 86 | Yes | none | Proof-free. Value is known to ledger state. |
| `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack` | 87 | Yes | 816 B | 128 B sigma (balance ownership, key linkage) + 688 B single Bulletproof |
| `ConfidentialMPTSend` | 88 | Yes | **946 B**, fixed | 192 B sigma (ciphertext consistency across sender/receiver/issuer/auditor, amount linkage, balance linkage) + 754 B aggregated Bulletproof over two 64-bit values |
| `ConfidentialMPTClawback` | 89 | Yes | 64 B | Sigma proof that `sfIssuerEncryptedBalance` encrypts the stated plaintext |

**~~Byte values are Grade B pending GAP-6.~~ Grade A as of 2026-08-16.** `Protocol.h:466–471` verifies the *structure* — `kEcSendProofLength = kEcSendSigmaProofLength + kEcDoubleBulletproofLength`, enforced at preflight. The macros it resolves to are now read at mpt-crypto `0.4.0-rc4`: `SECP256K1_COMPACT_STANDARD_PROOF_SIZE 192`, `kMPT_DOUBLE_BULLETPROOF_SIZE 754`, `kMPT_SINGLE_BULLETPROOF_SIZE 688`, `SECP256K1_COMPACT_CONVERTBACK_PROOF_SIZE 128`, `SECP256K1_COMPACT_CLAWBACK_PROOF_SIZE 64`, `kMPT_SCHNORR_PROOF_SIZE 64`. Every value in the table above is confirmed. The header additionally derives each sigma size from its scalar count — send is (e, z_m, z_r, z_b, z_rho, z_sk) ∈ Z_q⁶ = 192 B — so the numbers are internally cross-checked as well.

Field codes, needed to patch a binary codec:

```
sfConfidentialBalanceVersion    UINT32  69     sfZKProof                     VL 37
sfConfidentialOutstandingAmount UINT64  32     sfHolderEncryptedAmount       VL 38
sfBlindingFactor                UINT256 40     sfIssuerEncryptedAmount       VL 39
sfConfidentialBalanceInbox      VL      32     sfSenderEncryptedAmount       VL 40
sfConfidentialBalanceSpending   VL      33     sfDestinationEncryptedAmount  VL 41
sfIssuerEncryptedBalance        VL      34     sfAuditorEncryptedBalance     VL 42
sfIssuerEncryptionKey           VL      35     sfAuditorEncryptedAmount      VL 43
sfHolderEncryptionKey           VL      36     sfAuditorEncryptionKey        VL 44
                                               sfAmountCommitment            VL 45
                                               sfBalanceCommitment           VL 46
```

Structural details worth carrying forward:

- `ConfidentialMPTConvert` is `NotDelegable`; the other four are `Delegable`. You cannot delegate the opt-in that binds an identity to an encryption key.
- `ConfidentialMPTSend` carries `sfDestinationTag` — a plaintext correlation handle on a confidential transfer. Test it in the observer harness.
- `sfCredentialIDs` on Send is the XLS-70 hook.

## 4. The key decision

Recorded in full as **[ADR-0001](../decisions/ADR-0001-key-custody-and-proof-location.md)**, revised after review. Status `Proposed`; two of its arguments have been seen by no reviewer.

The finding that drives it: **in XLS-96, holder key custody controls spending authority, not privacy.** `sfIssuerEncryptedBalance` is mandatory on every confidential balance and `IssuerEncryptionKey` is required to use the feature at all. There is no configuration in which a holder is private from the issuer.

## 6. Cost

**Size. ~~Grade A on the total, B on the components~~ Grade A throughout, MEASURED ON THE WIRE 2026-08-17** (spec §14.1, `Nciphers = 4`): 264 B ciphertexts + 66 B Pedersen commitments + 946 B ZKProof = **1276 B with auditor, 1210 B without** — both figures confirmed by accepted Devnet transactions at n=4 and n=3 respectively, not by arithmetic. Signed blob 1492 B / 1423 B. **The competing 1177 B in `cmpt-compact-sigma.pdf` Table 2 is refuted for the wire**: `C₁` is shared, and protocol-enforced as shared, but transmitted once per participant. See CLAIMS.md E-4 and F-13. `kTxMaxSizeBytes = megabytes(1)` — **Grade A, executed**. Size is not a binding constraint.

*Open:* `kOversizeMetaDataCap = 5200`. Confidential state updates write ciphertexts into metadata for both parties plus mirrors. Whether that approaches the cap has not been checked. Check it before asserting anything about ledger impact.

**Fee. Grade A.** `Protocol.h:492` — `kConfidentialFeeMultiplier = 9`, passed by `ConfidentialMPTSend::calculateBaseFee`. RippleX docs independently give **100 drops** before load scaling for a single-signed confidential transaction, against 10 for a standard one; multi-signed is `10 × (10 + signatures)`. *The exact arithmetic relating the constant to the result was not verified — `Transactor::calculateBaseFee` was not read. Two sources agree on 100 drops; the mechanism is stated as inference.*

Fee escalation multiplies that base as it does any transaction. **The 10× fee floor, not byte count, is what a high-throughput confidential application budgets for.**
/**
 * check-web-hosted — architecture §6 step 9's gate: the HOSTED part of
 * `check-web-readonly`, run over the UPLOADED OUTPUT and its routing
 * configuration, never over the source (`ADR-0004`, "What phase 2 step 4's gate
 * must check").
 *
 *   bun run tools/check-web-readonly.ts --hosted <output root> --commit <sha>
 *
 * `<output root>` holds `.vercel/output/`. On a pass it writes
 * `.vercel/output/static/gate-verdict.json`, which the page's footer reads: a
 * digest of every other file, so a reader can tell what the gate passed.
 *
 * ⚠ **Gates in this repository have false-passed before they worked**
 * (`CLAIMS.md` E-165, E-182, E-226). So every run first copies the real output,
 * breaks the copy one way per control, and runs the SAME `runChecks()` over it;
 * each control names the check that must fire, and the unbroken copy must pass.
 * A control that fails stops the run with `CONTROL-FAILED`.
 *
 * ⚠ **It cannot check egress.** It reads files; a visitor's requests are not in
 * them (`ADR-0004`). `web/hosted/browser-check.ts` observes one browser's
 * requests, which is evidence about that browser and not a proof. The full list
 * of what this gate does not check is printed on every run.
 *
 * The last line is always `check-web-hosted: verdict=<WORD> exit=<N>`.
 */

import { createHash, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import { cpSync, existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, mkdtempSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the output

/** Every file under `.vercel/output`, by path relative to it. Symlinks refused. */
export function readOutput(root: string): Map<string, Buffer> {
  const base = join(root, ".vercel", "output");
  if (!existsSync(base)) throw new Error(`${base} does not exist`);
  const files = new Map<string, Buffer>();
  const walk = (rel: string) => {
    for (const name of readdirSync(join(base, rel)).sort()) {
      const r = rel ? `${rel}/${name}` : name;
      const st = lstatSync(join(base, r));
      if (st.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`a symlink at ${r}: the uploader may follow it`);
      if (st.isDirectory()) walk(r);
      else if (st.isFile()) files.set(r, readFileSync(join(base, r)));
      else throw new Error(`${r} is not a regular file`);
    }
  };
  walk("");
  return files;
}

const VERDICT = "static/gate-verdict.json";
const text = (b: Buffer) => b.toString("utf8");
const sha256 = (b: Buffer | string) => createHash("sha256").update(b).digest("hex");

/**
 * React escapes these in text; the wording is compared after undoing it. ⚠
 * Numeric references are decoded too, because an attribute written as
 * `&#47;&#47;host` is `//host` to a browser and passed the URL check while it
 * was not (`REVIEW-059` R2-3).
 */
const NAMED: Record<string, string> = { quot: '"', lt: "<", gt: ">", amp: "&", apos: "'", sol: "/", colon: ":", period: ".", Tab: "\t", NewLine: "\n", nbsp: "\u00a0" };
export function decodeEntities(s: string): string {
  // ⚠ ONE pass. Sequential replacements decoded `&#x26;#47;` twice, and an
  // out-of-range reference threw (`REVIEW-059` R3-4). A numeric reference may
  // omit its semicolon, as a browser allows; an unknown name is left as written.
  return s.replace(/&(?:#[xX]([0-9a-fA-F]+);?|#(\d+);?|([A-Za-z]+);)/g, (m, hex, dec, name) => {
    if (hex !== undefined || dec !== undefined) {
      const cp = hex !== undefined ? parseInt(hex, 16) : Number(dec);
      return cp === 0 || cp > 0x10ffff || (cp >= 0xd800 && cp <= 0xdfff) ? "\ufffd" : String.fromCodePoint(cp);
    }
    return Object.hasOwn(NAMED, name) ? NAMED[name] : m;
  });
}

/**
 * The inner HTML of every element whose opening tag matches `open`, with nested
 * elements of the same name balanced. A regex to the first closing tag would
 * stop inside a nested `div`.
 */
export function elementsInner(html: string, tag: string, open: RegExp): string[] {
  const out: string[] = [];
  const any = new RegExp(`<(/?)${tag}\\b[^>]*>`, "gi");
  for (const m of html.matchAll(new RegExp(open.source, open.flags.includes("g") ? open.flags : open.flags + "g"))) {
    const start = m.index! + m[0].length;
    any.lastIndex = start;
    let depth = 1, end = -1;
    for (let t = any.exec(html); t; t = any.exec(html)) {
      depth += t[1] ? -1 : 1;
      if (depth === 0) { end = t.index; break; }
    }
    if (end >= 0) out.push(html.slice(start, end));
  }
  return out;
}

/** HTML read as text: block elements spaced, inline elements removed with nothing in their place. */
export function blockText(html: string): string {
  return decodeEntities(
    html.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, "")
      .replace(/<\/?(?:p|div|li|br|tr|td|th|h[1-6]|section|footer|header|ul|ol|table|thead|tbody|dl|dt|dd)\b[^>]*>/gi, " ")
      .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ""),
  ).replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim();
}

/** A page's text as a reader sees it: no comments, no tags, entities undone. */
export function pageText(h: string): string {
  return decodeEntities(h.replace(/<script[\s\S]*?<\/script>/gi, " ").replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, "").replace(/<[^>]+>/g, " ")).replace(/\s+/g, " ");
}

/**
 * The three readings of a page an identifier check runs over. ⚠ The source
 * spelling alone let `&#114;Hb9…` and an address split by a `<span>` through
 * (`REVIEW-059` R3-1): so also the page decoded, and its text with tags removed
 * and nothing put in their place.
 */
function readings(h: string): string[] {
  const noComments = h.replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, "");
  return [h, decodeEntities(noComments), decodeEntities(noComments.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ""))];
}
/**
 * A figure labelled as decrypted or plaintext: D-H3 was ruled A, no issuer
 * figure, and no page decrypts anything. ⚠ `REVIEW-059c` answered R1-2's request
 * for an output regression with a disclaimer; round two ran *"Decrypted issuer
 * balance: 42"* and *"Issuer plaintext balance: 73"* and both passed (R2-2).
 * This finds a LABELLED figure; an unlabelled number is prose (printed limit 8).
 */
// ⚠ Round three found the first version a word list one word wide: *"decrypted
// issuer balance is 42"*, *"decrypted view … : 42"*, *"decrypts … to 42"* and
// *"42 (decrypted issuer balance)"* all passed (`REVIEW-059` R3-2, S3-1). Now:
// any number later in the same clause as *decrypt* or *plaintext*, except one
// that is part of a reference such as `P-9`, `E-241` or `#10`; and any number
// followed by a parenthetical naming either word.
const ISSUER_FIGURE = [
  /\b(?:decrypt\w*|plaintext)\b[^.!?;]{0,80}?(?<![A-Za-z]-|#|\w|\.)\d/i,
  /(?<![\w.#-])\d[\d,.]*\s*(?:[A-Za-z]+\s+){0,2}\(\s*[^)]{0,40}\b(?:decrypted|plaintext)\b[^)]{0,40}\)/i,
];

/**
 * The response headers the first route sets, exactly: no fewer, no others
 * (`REVIEW-059` S-3: two of the five the assembler sets were unchecked). The
 * policy itself is checked directive by directive in check 6.
 */
export const EXPECTED_HEADERS: Record<string, string | null> = {
  "Content-Security-Policy": null,
  "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
  "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
  "Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy": "same-origin",
  "Permissions-Policy": "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), interest-cohort=()",
};

export function runChecks(files: Map<string, Buffer>, want: Expect): Finding[] {
  const f: Finding[] = [];
  const add = (check: string, detail: string) => f.push({ check, detail });
  const paths = [...files.keys()].filter((p) => p !== VERDICT);
  const html = new Map(paths.filter((p) => p.endsWith(".html")).map((p) => [p, text(files.get(p)!)]));

  // 1. Inventory and provenance.

exec
/bin/zsh -lc "sed -n '240,460p' tools/check-web-hosted.ts; sed -n '460,700p' tools/check-web-hosted.ts; sed -n '1,150p' web/hosted/licence-notices.ts; find review-input -type f | head -25; command -v bun" in $USER_TMP/T/r060a.qD7Xey/repo
 succeeded in 0ms:
  // 1. Inventory and provenance.
  for (const p of paths) if (!ADMITTED.some((re) => re.test(p))) add("inventory", `${p} is not admitted by the provenance rule`);
  for (const p of HOSTED_PAGES) if (!files.has(PAGE_HTML(p))) add("inventory", `the page /${p} is missing`);

  // 2. No source maps.
  for (const p of paths) if (/sourceMappingURL|\.map$/.test(p) || /[#@]\s*sourceMappingURL=/.test(text(files.get(p)!))) add("no-source-maps", `${p} carries or references a source map`);

  // 3. No server code: no function, no middleware, routes to files only.
  for (const p of paths) if (p.startsWith("functions/") || p.includes("/functions/")) add("no-server-code", `${p} is a function`);
  let config: any = null;
  try { config = JSON.parse(text(files.get("config.json") ?? Buffer.from("null"))); } catch { add("no-server-code", "config.json is not JSON"); }
  if (!config || config.version !== 3) add("no-server-code", "config.json is missing or not Build Output API version 3");
  else {
    for (const k of Object.keys(config)) if (k !== "version" && k !== "routes") add("no-server-code", `config.json has a top-level key ${k}`);
    for (const [i, r] of (config.routes ?? []).entries()) {
      for (const k of Object.keys(r)) if (!["src", "dest", "headers", "continue", "handle"].includes(k)) add("no-server-code", `a route has the key ${k}`);
      // ⚠ Every reader of the policy (this gate, the browser check, the live
      // comparison) reads the FIRST route's headers. A later route's headers
      // would be read by none of them, so only the first may set any
      // (`REVIEW-059` S-1).
      if (i > 0 && r.headers !== undefined) add("csp", `route ${i} sets headers; only the first route may, because it is the only one any check reads`);
      if (r.handle !== undefined && r.handle !== "filesystem") add("no-server-code", `a route hands off to ${r.handle}`);
      if (r.dest !== undefined && (typeof r.dest !== "string" || !files.has(`static${r.dest}`))) add("no-server-code", `a route's dest ${JSON.stringify(r.dest)} is not a file in the output`);
    }
  }

  // 4. No socket client, signer path, decryption routine, secret name or build variable.
  const NEEDLES = [...SOCKET_NEEDLES, ...SECRET_NEEDLES, "WebAssembly", ".wasm", "ProjectivePoint", "mptool", "mpt_", "elgamal_", "VITE_", "WCONF_", "eval(", "new Function"];
  for (const p of paths) {
    if (p === "static/third-party-licenses.txt") continue;
    const t = text(files.get(p)!);
    for (const n of NEEDLES) if (t.includes(n)) add("no-socket-secret-or-decryption", `${p} contains ${JSON.stringify(n)}`);
    for (const api of ["new WebSocket", "EventSource(", "sendBeacon", "XMLHttpRequest"]) if (t.includes(api)) add("no-other-connection", `${p} uses ${api}`);
  }

  // 5. Absolute URLs, against the admitted list.
  for (const p of paths) {
    if (p === "static/third-party-licenses.txt") continue;
    for (const m of text(files.get(p)!).matchAll(/\bhttps?:\/\/[A-Za-z0-9.:/#_-]+/g)) {
      const u = m[0].replace(/[.:]+$/, "");
      if (!ADMITTED_URLS.some(([re]) => re.test(u))) add("urls", `${p} names ${u}`);
    }
  }
  // ⚠ A scheme-relative address (`src="//host/x.js"`) has no `https:` for the
  // pattern above to match (`REVIEW-059` R1-2's table), and an encoded one
  // (`&#47;&#47;host`, `https&#58;//host`) has neither (R2-3). So every
  // URL-bearing attribute is decoded first, and each `srcset` candidate is read.
  const URL_ATTRS = /\b(src|href|action|formaction|srcset|poster|data|background|xlink:href)\s*=\s*(?:"([^"]*)"|'([^']*)'|([^\s>]+))/gi;
  for (const [p, h] of html) {
    for (const m of h.matchAll(URL_ATTRS)) {
      const value = decodeEntities(m[2] ?? m[3] ?? m[4] ?? "").trim();
      const candidates = m[1].toLowerCase() === "srcset" ? value.split(",").map((c) => c.trim().split(/\s+/)[0]) : [value];
      // ⚠ Resolved, not prefix-tested: a tab between the slashes or a
      // backslash is `//` to a URL parser (`REVIEW-059` R3-3).
      for (const c of candidates) {
        const cleaned = c.replace(/[\t\n\r]/g, "");
        let u: URL;
        try { u = new URL(cleaned, SAME_ORIGIN); } catch { add("urls", `${p} has an attribute URL that does not parse: ${JSON.stringify(c)}`); continue; }
        if (u.origin === new URL(SAME_ORIGIN).origin) continue;
        if (/^[\\/]{2}/.test(cleaned)) add("urls", `${p} names the scheme-relative ${c}`);
        else if (!ADMITTED_URLS.some(([re]) => re.test(cleaned.replace(/[.:]+$/, "")) || re.test(u.href.replace(/\/$/, "")))) add("urls", `${p} names ${c} in an attribute`);
      }
    }
  }

  // 6. The Content Security Policy, as config.json delivers it.
  const first = config?.routes?.[0];
  const csp: string | undefined = first?.src === "/(.*)" && first?.continue === true ? first?.headers?.["Content-Security-Policy"] : undefined;
  if (!csp) add("csp", "the first route does not set a Content-Security-Policy on every path");
  else {
    // ⚠ A browser enforces the FIRST of two directives with one name and
    // ignores the second; a Map keeps the LAST. So `connect-src *;` placed
    // before the real one passed this check while the page permitted a
    // connection anywhere (`REVIEW-059` R1-1, measured). A repeated name, in
    // any case, is refused before anything else is read.
    const parsed = csp.split(";").map((d) => d.trim()).filter(Boolean).map((d) => { const [k, ...v] = d.split(/\s+/); return [k, v] as const; });
    const seen = new Set<string>();
    for (const [k] of parsed) { if (seen.has(k.toLowerCase())) add("csp", `the directive ${k} appears twice; a browser enforces the first`); seen.add(k.toLowerCase()); }
    const dirs = new Map(parsed);
    const exact: Record<string, string[]> = {
      "default-src": ["'self'"], "style-src": ["'self'"], "img-src": ["'self'"], "font-src": ["'self'"],
      "connect-src": ["'self'"], "object-src": ["'none'"], "base-uri": ["'none'"], "form-action": ["'none'"], "frame-ancestors": ["'none'"],
    };
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(exact)) if (JSON.stringify(dirs.get(k) ?? null) !== JSON.stringify(v)) add("csp", `${k} is ${JSON.stringify(dirs.get(k) ?? null)}, not ${v.join(" ")}`);
    for (const k of dirs.keys()) if (!(k in exact) && k !== "script-src") add("csp", `an unexpected directive ${k}`);
    const script = dirs.get("script-src") ?? [];
    if (script[0] !== "'self'") add("csp", "script-src does not start with 'self'");
    const allowed = new Set(script.slice(1));
    for (const tok of allowed) if (!/^'sha256-[A-Za-z0-9+/]+=*'$/.test(tok)) add("csp", `script-src admits ${tok}`);
    const needed = new Set([...html.values()].flatMap((h) => inlineScripts(h).map(scriptHash)));
    for (const h of needed) if (!allowed.has(h)) add("csp", `an inline script's hash ${h} is not admitted, so the page would not run`);
    for (const h of allowed) if (!needed.has(h)) add("csp", `script-src admits ${h}, which no page carries`);
    const names = Object.keys(first.headers ?? {});
    for (const n of names) if (!(n in EXPECTED_HEADERS)) add("csp", `the first route sets ${n}, which is not one of the expected headers`);
    const lower = names.map((n) => n.toLowerCase());
    if (new Set(lower).size !== lower.length) add("csp", "the first route sets one header name twice in different case");
    for (const [h, v] of Object.entries(EXPECTED_HEADERS)) if (v !== null && first.headers?.[h] !== v) add("csp", `${h} is not ${v}`);
  }
  for (const [p, h] of html) if (/\sstyle="|<style[\s>]/.test(h)) add("csp", `${p} carries inline style, which style-src 'self' refuses`);

  // 7. No input that asks a visitor for anything.
  for (const [p, h] of html) if (FORMS.test(h)) add("no-inputs", `${p} renders a form control`);

  // 8. Every ledger page renders the wording, the network check and the index,
  //    and no other page renders a ledger value.
  const indices = new Set<string>();
  const ledgerHtml = new Set(LEDGER_PAGES.map((lp) => PAGE_HTML(lp)));
  for (const lp of ledgerHtml) if (html.has(lp) && !html.get(lp)!.includes("data-ledger-value")) add("ledger-wording", `${lp} is a ledger page and marks no ledger value`);
  for (const [p, h] of html) {
    if (ledgerHtml.has(p)) continue;
    if (h.includes("data-ledger-value")) add("ledger-wording", `${p} marks a ledger value and is not one of the named ledger pages`);
    const r = readings(h);
    const first = (re: RegExp) => r.map((t) => t.match(re)?.[0]).find(Boolean);
    if (first(CIPHERTEXT)) add("ledger-wording", `${p} carries a ciphertext and is not one of the named ledger pages`);
    else if (first(HASH64)) add("ledger-wording", `${p} carries a 64-hex value, ${first(HASH64)}, and is not one of the named ledger pages`);
    const addr = first(ADDRESS) ?? first(X_ADDRESS);
    if (addr) add("ledger-wording", `${p} names an address, ${addr}, and is not one of the named ledger pages`);
    const iid = first(ISSUANCE_ID);
    if (iid) add("ledger-wording", `${p} names an issuance ID, ${iid}, and is not one of the named ledger pages`);
  }
  // 8b. No issuer figure, on any page (D-H3).
  for (const [p, h] of html) {
    const t = pageText(h);
    for (const re of ISSUER_FIGURE) { const m = t.match(re); if (m) add("no-issuer-figure", `${p} shows a labelled figure: ${JSON.stringify(m[0])}`); }
  }
  for (const [p, h] of html) {
    if (!ledgerHtml.has(p)) continue;
    const plain = decodeEntities(h);
    for (const para of DH2_WORDING) if (!plain.includes(para)) add("ledger-wording", `${p} renders a ledger value without the D-H2 sentence beginning ${JSON.stringify(para.slice(0, 40))}`);
    if (!h.includes(`data-network-id="${DEVNET_NETWORK_ID}"`)) add("ledger-wording", `${p} renders a ledger value without the Devnet network check`);
    const idx = h.match(/data-ledger-index="(\d+)"/);
    if (!idx) add("ledger-wording", `${p} renders a ledger value without the ledger index`);
    else indices.add(idx[1]);
  }
  if (indices.size > 1) add("ledger-wording", `pages name different ledgers: ${[...indices].join(", ")}`);
  for (const [p, label] of [["static/observer/index.html", "Observer view: "], ["static/issuer/index.html", "Issuer&#x27;s copy: "]] as const) {
    const n = (html.get(p) ?? "").split(label).length - 1;
    if (html.has(p) && n !== DEMO_ACCOUNTS.length) add("accounts", `${p} renders ${n} account panels, not ${DEMO_ACCOUNTS.length}`);
  }

  // 9. The commit and the verdict, on every page.
  for (const [p, h] of html) {
    if (!h.includes(`/commit/${want.commit}`)) add("commit-and-verdict", `${p} does not name commit ${want.commit}`);
    // A link into the repository at any commit but the build's would cite text the gate never saw.
    for (const m of h.matchAll(/xrpl-confidential-positions\/(?:commit|blob)\/([0-9a-f]{40})/g)) {
      if (m[1] !== want.commit) add("commit-and-verdict", `${p} links the repository at ${m[1].slice(0, 12)}, not the build's commit`);
    }
    if (!h.includes(`<code>${want.commit.slice(0, 12)}</code>`)) add("commit-and-verdict", `${p} does not show commit ${want.commit.slice(0, 12)} as its link text`);
    if (!h.includes("data-gate-verdict")) add("commit-and-verdict", `${p} has no gate-verdict slot`);
  }

  // 10. Licence notices for what is bundled, and nothing that should never be.
  const lic = files.get("static/third-party-licenses.txt");
  if (!lic) add("licences", "static/third-party-licenses.txt is missing");
  else {
    // Separator, `name@version (licence)`, separator, licence text: split on the
    // separator lines, so each header is followed by its own body.
    const parts = text(lic).split(/^={20,}$/m);
    // ⚠ The text before the first notice, and any part after the last one,
    // were read by no check (`REVIEW-059` S-4). The first must be the build's
    // fixed header; there must be no second.
    if (parts[0].trim() !== LICENCE_FILE_HEADER.join("\n").trim()) add("licences", "the text before the first notice is not the build's fixed header");
    if (parts.length % 2 === 0) add("licences", "the file has text after its last notice");
    const names: [string, string, string][] = [];
    for (let i = 1; i + 1 < parts.length; i += 2) {
      const head = parts[i].trim().match(/^((?:@[^/\s]+\/)?[^@\s]+)@\S+ \([^)]*\)$/);
      if (!head) { add("licences", `an entry header is malformed: ${JSON.stringify(parts[i].trim().slice(0, 60))}`); continue; }
      names.push([head[0], head[1], parts[i + 1]]);
    }
    // Each notice must be the package's own licence file with only its email
    // addresses removed (E-335), read from this checkout's node_modules at the
    // same version. A version this checkout does not hold cannot be verified.
    for (const [header, name, body] of names) {
      const root = join(REPO, "node_modules", name);
      const version = header.slice(name.length + 1, header.indexOf(" "));
      const have = existsSync(join(root, "package.json")) ? JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, "package.json"), "utf8")).version : null;
      if (have !== version) { add("licences", `${name}@${version} cannot be verified: this checkout's node_modules holds ${have ?? "nothing"}`); continue; }
      if (shippedNotice(root) !== body.trim()) add("licences", `${name}'s notice is not its own licence file with only email addresses removed`);
    }
    if (names.length === 0) add("licences", "the licence file lists no package");
    for (const [, name, body] of names) {
      if (!ADMITTED_PACKAGES.has(name)) add("licences", `the bundle contains ${name}, which is not admitted`);
      if (body.trim().length < 100) add("licences", `${name}'s licence text is missing or truncated`);
    }
    // ⚠ Only React and React DOM were required, so deleting seroval's whole
    // entry passed (`REVIEW-059` R1-4). The listed set must equal the admitted
    // set: a package the framework stops bundling is removed here in review,
    // as one it starts bundling is added.
    for (const must of ADMITTED_PACKAGES) if (!names.some((m) => m[1] === must)) add("licences", `${must} is admitted and not listed, so a bundled package may be shipped without its notice`);
  }
  return f;
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ the secret scan

/**
 * `check-no-secrets --dir`, with the local store. Its verdict line is required.
 *
 * ⚠ It reads a copy WITHOUT `static/gate-verdict.json`, the file this gate writes
 * after the sweep. Re-running the gate on its own output failed whenever Vite's
 * hash put `Sk` in an asset's name, because the sweep reads the digest beside that
 * name as a labelled scalar (`REVIEW-059` R3-12, measured). Every other file is
 * read as before.
 */
export function secretScan(root: string): { ok: boolean; line: string } {
  const copy = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "check-web-hosted-sweep-"));
  try {
    cpSync(join(root, ".vercel", "output"), join(copy, "output"), { recursive: true });
    rmSync(join(copy, "output", VERDICT), { force: true });
    return sweep(join(copy, "output"));
  } finally {
    rmSync(copy, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
}

function sweep(dir: string): { ok: boolean; line: string } {
  const r = Bun.spawnSync(["bun", "run", join(REPO, "tools/check-no-secrets.ts"), "--dir", dir], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" });
  const lines = r.stdout.toString().trim().split("\n");
  const last = lines[lines.length - 1] ?? "";
  return { ok: last === "check-no-secrets: verdict=PASS exit=0" && r.exitCode === 0, line: last };
}
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ controls

type Mutate = (dir: string) => void;
const out = (dir: string, p: string) => join(dir, ".vercel", "output", p);
const edit = (dir: string, p: string, fn: (s: string) => string) => writeFileSync(out(dir, p), fn(readFileSync(out(dir, p), "utf8")));
const firstJs = (dir: string) => "static/assets/" + readdirSync(out(dir, "static/assets")).find((n) => n.endsWith(".js"))!;
const editConfig = (dir: string, fn: (c: any) => void) => edit(dir, "config.json", (s) => { const c = JSON.parse(s); fn(c); return JSON.stringify(c); });

const LIC = "static/third-party-licenses.txt";
const csp = (d: string, fn: (p: string) => string) => editConfig(d, (c) => (c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = fn(c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"])));
const WEAK_POLICY = "default-src *; script-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'; connect-src *";

/**
 * Each control: what it breaks, the check that must fire and, where a check
 * has several reasons to fire, the words its finding must contain. ⚠ Without
 * the last, a control can pass on a finding next to the one it is named for:
 * the cryptography-package control fired because its fabricated notice did not
 * match a licence file, and kept passing with the admission rule deleted
 * (`REVIEW-059` R1-3).
 */
export const CONTROLS: [string, string, Mutate, string?][] = [
  ["a stray file", "inventory", (d) => writeFileSync(out(d, "static/notes.txt"), "x")],
  ["a source map", "inventory", (d) => writeFileSync(out(d, "static/assets/app.js.map"), "{}")],
  ["a sourceMappingURL comment", "no-source-maps", (d) => edit(d, firstJs(d), (s) => s + "\n//# sourceMappingURL=app.js.map\n")],
  ["a missing page", "inventory", (d) => rmSync(out(d, "static/issuer/index.html"))],
  ["a serverless function", "no-server-code", (d) => { const p = out(d, "functions/api.func"); mkdirSync(p, { recursive: true }); writeFileSync(join(p, ".vc-config.json"), "{}"); }],
  ["middleware in config.json", "no-server-code", (d) => editConfig(d, (c) => c.routes.unshift({ src: "/(.*)", middlewarePath: "_middleware" }))],
  ["a rewrite to another host", "no-server-code", (d) => editConfig(d, (c) => c.routes.splice(1, 0, { src: "/x", dest: "https://example.com/x" }))],
  ["a top-level overrides key", "no-server-code", (d) => editConfig(d, (c) => (c.overrides = {}))],
  ["the signer socket path in a script", "no-socket-secret-or-decryption", (d) => edit(d, firstJs(d), (s) => s + ';const p="/run/wconf/signer.sock";')],
  ["a WebAssembly module", "no-socket-secret-or-decryption", (d) => edit(d, firstJs(d), (s) => s + ";WebAssembly.instantiate(x);")],
  ["a build variable inlined", "no-socket-secret-or-decryption", (d) => edit(d, firstJs(d), (s) => s + ';const v="VITE_WCONF_WEB_PORT";')],
  ["a WebSocket", "no-other-connection", (d) => edit(d, firstJs(d), (s) => s + ';new WebSocket("wss://x");')],
  ["a third-party URL", "urls", (d) => edit(d, "static/index.html", (s) => s.replace("</body>", '<a href="https://analytics.example.net/x">x</a></body>'))],
  ["'unsafe-inline' in script-src", "csp", (d) => editConfig(d, (c) => (c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"].replace("script-src 'self'", "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'")))],
  ["a widened connect-src", "csp", (d) => editConfig(d, (c) => (c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"].replace("connect-src 'self'", "connect-src 'self' https://s.devnet.rippletest.net:51234")))],
  ["an inline script the policy does not admit", "csp", (d) => edit(d, "static/index.html", (s) => s.replace("</body>", "<script>window.x=1</script></body>"))],
  ["no policy at all", "csp", (d) => editConfig(d, (c) => delete c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"])],
  // ⚠ The first build hashed the file's bytes; the browser hashes the parsed
  // text, refused every page's hydration script, and this gate had passed it.
  ["a script carrying NUL, admitted by its RAW hash", "csp", (d) => {
    const raw = "window.y='\u0000'";
    edit(d, "static/index.html", (s) => s.replace("</body>", `<script>${raw}</script></body>`));
    const rawHash = `'sha256-${createHash("sha256").update(raw, "utf8").digest("base64")}'`;
    editConfig(d, (c) => (c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = c.routes[0].headers["Content-Security-Policy"].replace("script-src 'self'", `script-src 'self' ${rawHash}`)));
  }],
  ["an inline style attribute", "csp", (d) => edit(d, "static/index.html", (s) => s.replace("<body>", '<body><div style="color:red">x</div>'))],
  ["an input asking for a seed", "no-inputs", (d) => edit(d, "static/index.html", (s) => s.replace("</body>", '<input name="seed"></body>'))],

export function runControls(root: string, want: Expect): { run: number; failed: string[] } {
  const failed: string[] = [];
  let run = 0;
  const fresh = () => { const d = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "check-web-hosted-")); cpSync(join(root, ".vercel"), join(d, ".vercel"), { recursive: true }); return d; };
  const dirs: string[] = [];
  try {
    const clean = fresh(); dirs.push(clean);
    run++;
    const base = runChecks(readOutput(clean), want);
    if (base.length) failed.push(`the unbroken copy must pass, and has ${base.length} finding(s): ${base[0].check}: ${base[0].detail}`);
    for (const [name, check, mutate, detail] of CONTROLS) {
      const d = fresh(); dirs.push(d);
      run++;
      mutate(d);
      const got = runChecks(readOutput(d), want);
      if (!got.some((x) => x.check === check && (!detail || x.detail.includes(detail)))) failed.push(`${name}: expected a '${check}' finding${detail ? ` saying "${detail}"` : ""}, got ${got.length ? got.map((x) => `${x.check}: ${x.detail}`).join(" | ") : "none"}`);
    }
    // The secret scan, through the same function the real check calls.
    const d = fresh(); dirs.push(d);
    run++;
    edit(d, firstJs(d), (s) => s + `;const s="${plantedSeed()}";`);
    if (secretScan(d).ok) failed.push("a seed planted in a script: check-no-secrets --dir passed it");
  } finally {
    for (const d of dirs) rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
  return { run, failed };
}

/** A real-entropy ed25519 seed, made at run time so this file holds none. */
function plantedSeed(): string {
  return encodeSeed(randomBytes(16), "ed25519");
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ disclosure

export function whatThisDoesNotCheck(): string[] {
  return [
    "1. EGRESS. It reads files; what a visitor's browser sends is not in them. The policy's connect-src 'self' is checked as written, not as a browser enforces it.",
    "2. The SERVED bytes and headers. It checks the output before upload; step 7 of web/hosted/README.md compares the deployed site with gate-verdict.json, and that comparison detects a change at the moment it runs, nothing later.",
    "3. The BUILD MACHINE. An inventory of the output cannot show that the build never read a private store, or that every file came from the named commit; the isolated build and its tree check are what address that.",
    "4. Whether the PROSE is true. Wording is claims-check's and the wording tests' question; this gate checks that the ruled D-H2 sentences are present, not that every other sentence is right.",
    "5. Anything a script asks a visitor for after hydration, by a form control or a dialog such as prompt(). The check reads the prerendered HTML; React's DOM code names input elements internally, so the bundle cannot be read for them.",
    "6. A decryption routine under a name it does not list. It forbids WebAssembly, the named mpt-crypto and ElGamal identifiers and any cryptography package in the licence list, which is a named set.",
    "7. A package inlined without its module path. The licence list is collected from the module graph the build reported, and the gate requires that list to equal the admitted set.",
    "8. A ledger value on a page outside /observer and /issuer is found only if it is a ciphertext, a 64-hex value, a classic or X-address, an issuance ID or a marked value, read in the source, decoded, and with tags removed; a figure written as prose is not.",
    "9. NO ISSUER FIGURE (D-H3): the build container holds no key, so no figure can be computed. This gate refuses a number in the same clause after 'decrypt' or 'plaintext', or followed by a parenthetical naming either, on any page. That is a pattern, not an understanding of the sentence: a figure phrased another way is prose, and code that runs during the build could write one (item 3).",
  ];
}

// ------------------------------------------------------------------ main

export function verdictFile(files: Map<string, Buffer>, want: Expect, controls: number) {
  const entries = [...files].filter(([p]) => p !== VERDICT).sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b));
  const perFile = Object.fromEntries(entries.map(([p, b]) => [p, sha256(b)]));
  return {
    verdict: "PASS",
    gate: "check-web-readonly --hosted (tools/check-web-hosted.ts)",
    checkedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    commit: want.commit,
    controls,
    files: entries.length,
    outputDigest: sha256(entries.map(([p, b]) => `${p}\t${sha256(b)}`).join("\n")),
    perFile,
    doesNotCheck: whatThisDoesNotCheck(),
  };
}

export async function runHosted(argv: string[]): Promise<number> {
  const finish = (word: string, exit: number) => { console.log(`check-web-hosted: verdict=${word} exit=${exit}`); return exit; };
  try {
    const at = argv.indexOf("--hosted"), ct = argv.indexOf("--commit");
    const root = argv[at + 1], commit = argv[ct + 1];
    if (!root || root.startsWith("--")) throw new Error("--hosted needs the output root, the directory that holds .vercel/output");
    if (!commit || !/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/.test(commit)) throw new Error("--commit needs the full public commit id the build ran from");
    const want = { commit };
    console.log(`check-web-hosted over ${join(root, ".vercel/output")}, expecting commit ${commit}`);

    const c = runControls(root, want);
    console.log(`controls: ${c.run - c.failed.length}/${c.run} passed, each through the same runChecks() and secretScan() as the real check`);
    if (c.failed.length) { for (const x of c.failed) console.log(`  CONTROL FAILED: ${x}`); return finish("CONTROL-FAILED", 2); }

    const files = readOutput(root);
    const findings = runChecks(files, want);
    const secrets = secretScan(root);
    if (!secrets.ok) findings.push({ check: "secrets", detail: `check-no-secrets --dir: ${secrets.line}` });
    console.log(`scanned: ${[...files.keys()].filter((p) => p !== VERDICT).length} file(s); secret sweep: ${secrets.line}`);
    console.log("\nWhat this gate does NOT check:");
    for (const l of whatThisDoesNotCheck()) console.log(`  ${l}`);
    if (findings.length) {
      console.log(`\nFAILING: ${findings.length}`);
      for (const x of findings) console.log(`  ${x.check}: ${x.detail}`);
      return finish("FAIL", 1);
    }
    const v = verdictFile(files, want, c.run);
    writeFileSync(join(root, ".vercel/output", VERDICT), JSON.stringify(v, null, 2) + "\n");
    console.log(`\nwrote ${VERDICT}: ${v.files} files, output digest ${v.outputDigest}`);
    return finish("PASS", 0);
  } catch (e) {
    console.log(`REFUSED: ${String(e)}`);
    return finish("REFUSED", 2);
  }
}

if (import.meta.main) process.exit(await runHosted(process.argv.slice(2)));
/**
 * The licence notices shipped with the hosted bundle, shared by the build's
 * plugin (`web/app/vite.hosted.config.ts`) and the gate, so both read one rule.
 *
 * ⚠ **Email addresses are removed from the shipped notices, and only those.**
 * seroval's MIT notice, which TanStack Start bundles, names its author's
 * personal address, and this repository does not republish personal addresses
 * (`check-no-secrets`'s email class). The project owner ruled on 2026-10-20 to
 * keep each notice and replace the address with a marker; the copyright line
 * keeps its year and holder (`CLAIMS.md` E-335). The gate checks that every
 * shipped notice is the package's own licence file with that one change.
 */
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";

export const EMAIL_MARKER = "[email address removed; the package's own licence file carries it]";

/**
 * The licence file's opening lines, before the first notice. One constant, so
 * the gate can require the file to open with exactly this and nothing else
 * (`REVIEW-059` S-4: the region before the first notice was read by no check).
 */
export const LICENCE_FILE_HEADER = [
  "Third-party software in the W-CONF hosted demo's client bundle, with the licence",
  "each package ships. Collected at build time from the modules actually bundled.",
  `Email addresses in these notices are replaced with "${EMAIL_MARKER}".`,
  "",
];
const EMAIL = /[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/g;

export function redactEmails(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(EMAIL, EMAIL_MARKER);
}

const LICENCE_FILES = ["LICENSE", "LICENSE.md", "LICENSE.txt", "license", "license.md", "LICENCE"];

/** A package root's licence file, or null. */
export function licenceFileOf(root: string): string | null {
  return LICENCE_FILES.map((f) => join(root, f)).find(existsSync) ?? null;
}

/** The notice as it is shipped: the package's licence file, emails removed, trailing space trimmed. */
export function shippedNotice(root: string): string | null {
  const f = licenceFileOf(root);
  return f ? redactEmails(readFileSync(f, "utf8")).trimEnd() : null;
}

/**
 * What the issuer can read, without the figure: `ADR-0004` D-H3, ruled A
 * (`CLAIMS.md` E-331).
 *
 * ⚠ **Every value here is a ledger reading.** The page shows that each
 * holder's `IssuerEncryptedBalance` is on the ledger and the issuance key the
 * protocol encrypts it under. It does not show a decrypted balance: E-241's
 * reasoning holds with more force on a public page, because a figure no visitor
 * can check is a claim with no falsifier.
 */
function Issuer() {
  const iss = SNAPSHOT.issuance;
  return (
    <>
      <Panel title="A holder is never private from the issuer" tone="warn">
        <p className="text-sm leading-relaxed">
          The protocol keeps a second copy of every confidential balance, the
          {" "}<code>IssuerEncryptedBalance</code>, encrypted to the issuer&rsquo;s key. The issuer can
          always decrypt it, and no setting turns this off (CLAIMS.md P-9).
        </p>
        <p className="text-sm leading-relaxed mt-2">
          This page shows that each copy is on the ledger. It does not show the decrypted figures: a
          visitor could not check them, so this project does not publish them (ADR-0004 D-H3).
        </p>
      </Panel>

      <LedgerReading />

      <Panel title="The issuance">
        {iss.exists ? (
          <div className="text-sm space-y-1">
            <div><span className="opacity-60">MPTokenIssuanceID</span> <code className="break-all" data-ledger-value="">{iss.id}</code></div>
            <div><span className="opacity-60">issuer</span> <code data-ledger-value="">{iss.issuer}</code></div>
            <div>
              <span className="opacity-60">IssuerEncryptionKey</span>{" "}
              <code className="text-[10px] break-all" data-ledger-value="">{iss.issuerEncryptionKey ?? "absent"}</code>
            </div>
          </div>
        ) : (
          <AbsentReading state="issuance-missing" />
        )}
      </Panel>

      {SNAPSHOT.accounts.map((a) => (
        <Panel key={a.address} title={`Issuer's copy: ${a.label}`}>
          <AccountHeading address={a.address} note={a.note} />
          {a.state === "present" && a.issuerMirror ? (
            a.issuerMirror.present ? (
              <div className="text-sm space-y-2">
                <div>
                  <span className="opacity-60">IssuerEncryptedBalance</span>{" "}
                  <code className="text-[10px] break-all block my-1 opacity-80" data-ledger-value="">{a.issuerMirror.ciphertext}</code>
                </div>
                <p>
                  Present, encrypted to the <code>IssuerEncryptionKey</code> above. It is a different
                  ciphertext from the holder&rsquo;s own balance.
                </p>
              </div>
            ) : (
              <p className="text-sm" data-ledger-value="">
                At validated ledger {SNAPSHOT.source.ledgerIndex} this position carries no
                {" "}<code>IssuerEncryptedBalance</code>.
              </p>
            )
          ) : (
            <AbsentReading state={a.state} />
          )}
        </Panel>
      ))}
    </>
  );
}
