PAGE custody 
  W-CONF: confidential MPT on the XRPL Devnet Devnet snapshot · signs nothing, holds no keys · not secure, not audited, not production-ready (P-5) W-CONF What confidential MPT on the XRP Ledger hides, and what it does not. A research project, shown on one snapshot of the Devnet. Overview How it works What anyone sees What the issuer sees Who can do what Wallets Custody This is a simulation No custody platform is integrated behind this page: no MPC, no HSM, no Harmonize. It models a key-source shape, a standalone ElGamal key plus an external signer, to show which flows survive and which break. Two findings 1. The derived key does not work with custodial key management The ElGamal secret is derived from the master seed, and a custody platform never releases the seed. So the account cannot derive its own ElGamal key or read its own confidential balance outside the platform. A platform that ran the derivation inside its own boundary would change that; it would need the derivation published as a standard, and it is not (issue #10). A standalone ElGamal key gets around this, but then something outside the custody platform holds a permanent decryption key. Who that should be is an open question in this project (CLAIMS.md E-117). 2. Approval policies cannot read a confidential amount An approval workflow that holds only public data sees a proof, not a value, so a rule like “two approvers above $1M” has nothing to check. This is structural, not an integration detail: confidentiality and amount-based approval policies pull against each other. The ways out each cost something: give the policy engine the ElGamal secret, and it becomes another party that reads every balance; accept the holder’s statement of the amount, and the policy rests on the holder’s honesty; or prove the bound in zero knowledge, which this project has neither built nor costed. Which flows survive, and which break Each flow lists what it needs, and the verdict is computed from what a custody-shaped key source has. Note 1: Only with a standalone ElGamal key, held outside the custody platform (E-117). survives: Send a public XRPL payment breaks: Onboard with the ruled derived key Structural in this simulation: a custody platform never releases seed material, so the account cannot derive its own ElGamal key outside the platform. A platform that ran the derivation inside its own boundary would change this, and that needs the derivation published (issue #10). survives: Onboard with a standalone ElGamal key (note 1) survives: Read own confidential balance (note 1) survives: Send a confidential amount (note 1) breaks: Send confidentially, under an amount-capped approval policy (note 1) Structural: the transaction carries a proof, not a value, so a rule like 'two approvers above $1M' has no amount to read. It is hidden from this simulation's policy engine too, which holds only public data. survives: Send confidentially, under a destination-allowlist policy (note 1) survives: Retire a position in tranches (note 1) Each tranche size and its timing is public: the amount is plaintext on every ConvertBack (CLAIMS.md F-24). | E-87 | ⚠ **A real defect in the signing path was found by a test, not by review, and it would have been rejected by every validator.** `SigningPubKey` is a **signing field**, and the first draft of `session::prove_confirm_and_sign` added it *after* computing the digest — so the signature covered a serialisation the blob did not contain. Found by `tests/signing_path.rs::the_signature_verifies_over_the_blob_that_carries_it`, which verifies the signature against the bytes **in the returned blob** rather than against the bytes the function happened to hold. /**
 * devnet-clean-account.ts — fire architecture §6 step 4's own falsifier.
 *
 * `observer-harness.ts --assert-no-r-reuse` is the falsifier step 4 names, and
 * `CLAIMS.md` E-76 records that it **had never been run against a transaction
 * this project's own code produced**. It could not be: nothing signed.
 *
 * It cannot be run against the 2026-08-17 holder either, because that account's
 * history contains the **deliberately broken** transactions of E-63 — two Sends
 * that reuse `r` on purpose, to demonstrate the attack. The assertion fires on
 * them, correctly, and would fire whatever this signer did.
 *
 * So this script builds a **clean** confidential holder whose every confidential
 * transaction is produced by `signer/`, and runs the assertion against that.
 * A pass there means something; a pass on a contaminated account would not, and
 * a *fail* on a contaminated account says nothing about our signer.
 *
 * ⚠ **Throwaway spike code. Devnet only.**
 *
 *   bun tools/spike-step3-2026-08-18/devnet-clean-account.ts [--auto-confirm]
 */
import { connect, rpc, close, state, save, tool, submit, sequenceOf, faucet } from "../spike-2026-08-17/convert.ts";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const AUTO = process.argv.includes("--auto-confirm");
const CONVERT_AMOUNT = 400;
const SEND_AMOUNT = 11;
const WORK = "/tmp/wconf/step3-clean";
const SOCKET = `${WORK}/signer.sock`;
const SIGNER = new URL("../../signer/target/debug/wconf-signer", import.meta.url).pathname;
const LABEL = "step3Holder";

const die = (m: string) => { console.error(`\n✗ ${m}`); process.exit(1); };

await connect();
const issuer = state.issuer, holderB = state.holderB;
if (!issuer || !holderB || !state.issuanceId) die("state.json is missing the 2026-08-17 setup");

const who = await faucet(LABEL);
console.log(`clean holder: ${who.address}`);

async function mptOf(addr: string) {
  const objs = await rpc({ command: "account_objects", account: addr, ledger_index: "validated", type: "mptoken" });
  return (objs.result.account_objects ?? []).find((o: any) => o.MPTokenIssuanceID === state.issuanceId);
}

// --- setup, all NON-confidential and all done here, not by the signer -------
if (!(await mptOf(who.address))) {
  const r = await submit({ TransactionType: "MPTokenAuthorize", MPTokenIssuanceID: state.issuanceId }, who.seed);
  if (!r.engine.startsWith("tes")) die(`authorize failed: ${r.engine}`);
}
let mpt = await mptOf(who.address);
if (Number(mpt.MPTAmount ?? 0) < CONVERT_AMOUNT) {
  const r = await submit({
    TransactionType: "Payment",
    Destination: who.address,
    Amount: { mpt_issuance_id: state.issuanceId, value: String(CONVERT_AMOUNT * 2) },
  }, issuer.seed);
  if (!r.engine.startsWith("tes")) die(`issuer payment failed: ${r.engine}`);
  mpt = await mptOf(who.address);
}
console.log(`public MPT balance: ${mpt.MPTAmount}`);

if (!state[`${LABEL}ElGamal`]) {
  const [sk, pk] = await tool("keygen");
  state[`${LABEL}ElGamal`] = { sk, pk }; save();
}
const eg = state[`${LABEL}ElGamal`];

const iss = (await rpc({ command: "ledger_entry", mpt_issuance: state.issuanceId, ledger_index: "validated" })).result?.node;
const bHolder = await mptOf(holderB.address);
if (!bHolder?.HolderEncryptionKey) die("holderB has no registered encryption key");

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The signer, driven twice: a Convert that registers the key, then a Send.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
rmSync(WORK, { recursive: true, force: true });
mkdirSync(WORK, { recursive: true });

let child: any = null;
let sock: any = null;
let buffer = "";
const inbox: string[] = [];

async function startSigner(profile: Record<string, unknown>) {
  writeFileSync(`${WORK}/profile.json`, JSON.stringify(profile, null, 2));
  child = spawn(SIGNER, [], {
    env: { ...process.env, WCONF_SIGNER_PROFILE: `${WORK}/profile.json`, WCONF_SIGNER_SOCKET: SOCKET, WCONF_SIGNER_STORE: `${WORK}/randomness` },
    stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
  });
  child.stdout.on("data", (d: any) => process.stdout.write(`  [signer] ${d}`));
  child.stderr.on("data", (d: any) => process.stderr.write(`  [signer] ${d}`));
  for (let i = 0; i < 50 && !existsSync(SOCKET); i++) await Bun.sleep(100);
  if (!existsSync(SOCKET)) die("the signer never created its socket");
  await Bun.sleep(300);
  buffer = ""; inbox.length = 0;
  sock = await Bun.connect({
    unix: SOCKET,
    socket: { data(_s: any, data: any) {
      buffer += data.toString();
      let i; while ((i = buffer.indexOf("\n")) >= 0) { inbox.push(buffer.slice(0, i)); buffer = buffer.slice(i + 1); }
    } },
  });
}

async function ask(req: unknown, confirm = false): Promise<any> {
  sock.write(JSON.stringify(req) + "\n");
  if (confirm && AUTO) { await Bun.sleep(1500); child.stdin.write("CONFIRM\n"); }
  for (let i = 0; i < 1200; i++) { if (inbox.length) return JSON.parse(inbox.shift()!); await Bun.sleep(100); }
  die("the signer did not answer");
}

function stopSigner() { try { sock?.end(); } catch {} child?.kill(); rmSync(SOCKET, { force: true }); }

async function ledgerNow() {
  return (await rpc({ command: "ledger_current" })).result.ledger_current_index + 20;
}

async function driveOne(op: string, amount: number, extra: Record<string, unknown>, profileOverrides: Record<string, unknown>) {
  // ⚠ **Secrets and policy only, as of 2026-08-19.** Architecture §6 step 2:
  // the balance ciphertext, the balance version, the registration state, the
  // issuer and auditor keys, the sequence, the last-ledger bound and the
  // destination's HolderEncryptionKey are all read **by the signer**, from a
  // node, at one pinned validated index. This function used to compute every
  // one of them — including a canonical-EncZero fallback for a holder with no
  // spending balance yet, which the signer now simply reads as absent.
  const profile = {
    account_seed: who.seed,
    elgamal_sk: eg.sk,
/**
 * devnet-signer-send.ts — **the objective of architecture §6 step 3.**
 *
 * Everything cryptographic is done by the Rust signer: the ruled `r`/`ρ`
 * derivation, the randomness ledger, the vendored prover, canonical XRPL
 * serialisation and the transaction signature. This file hands the signer its
 * **secrets**, asks it over a Unix socket, and submits the blob it gets back.
 * **It signs nothing and it holds no proof.**
 *
 * ## ⚠ ~~This file reads public ledger state~~ — it does not, as of 2026-08-19
 *
 * Architecture §6 **step 2** is built. The signer reads its own sequence
 * number, confidential balance, `ConfidentialBalanceVersion`, registration
 * state, the issuer and auditor keys and the destination's
 * `HolderEncryptionKey` from a node, at one pinned validated index, and
 * **re-reads before signing**. None of it is in the profile any more, and a
 * profile that still carries any of it fails to load by name.
 *
 * What this file still reads is what it needs for **its own** decisions: does
 * the inbox need merging before there is anything to send, and did the
 * submitted transaction validate. Those are the harness's questions, not the
 * signer's.
 *
 * ⚠ **Throwaway spike code. Devnet only** — it refuses any `network_id` but 2.
 *
 * ## What this does NOT establish
 *
 * A `tesSUCCESS` says the ledger accepted the transaction. It says nothing
 * about confidentiality: amounts are hidden, identities, counterparties,
 * timing and frequency are not, and the issuer can decrypt every amount
 * (`CLAIMS.md` P-4, P-9, P-11). `observer-harness.ts` is what shows that, and
 * this script prints the command rather than implying it ran.
 *
 * ## Two honest limitations, stated because they are easy to miss
 *
 * 1. **This script knows the holder's seed.** It writes it into the profile the
 *    signer reads. A real deployment would have the key reach the signer some
 *    other way; a throwaway-key spike cannot demonstrate that and does not
 *    pretend to.
 * 2. **`--auto-confirm` types CONFIRM into the signer's stdin.** That is the
 *    operator's own script driving the operator's own terminal, and it is
 *    still not a human reading the confirmation. Run without the flag to
 *    confirm by hand, which is what the boundary is actually for.
 *
 *   bun tools/spike-step3-2026-08-18/devnet-signer-send.ts [--auto-confirm] [--amount N]
 */
import { connect, rpc, close, state, save, tool, submit, sequenceOf, accountIdHex } from "../spike-2026-08-17/convert.ts";
import { spawn } from "node:child_process";
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";

const AUTO = process.argv.includes("--auto-confirm");
const AMOUNT = Number(process.argv.find((a) => a.startsWith("--amount="))?.split("=")[1] ?? 25);
const WORK = "/tmp/wconf/step3";
const SOCKET = "/tmp/wconf/step3/signer.sock";  // its own directory: the signer sets it 0700
const SIGNER = new URL("../../signer/target/debug/wconf-signer", import.meta.url).pathname;

const die = (m: string) => { console.error(`\n✗ ${m}`); process.exit(1); };

await connect();

const holder = state.holder, holderB = state.holderB;
if (!holder || !holderB || !state.issuanceId) die("state.json has no holder/holderB/issuance. Run the 2026-08-17 spike first.");

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1. ~~Public ledger state. The signer does not read the ledger — architecture
//    §6 step 2 is not built — so this is where that gap is filled, visibly.~~
//
//    **Step 2 is built.** What is left here is the harness's own setup: a
//    freshly-merged balance is the canonical EncZero and there is nothing to
//    send, so the inbox is merged first. The signer does not implement
//    MergeInbox and this is not it filling a gap on the signer's behalf.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
async function mptOf(addr: string) {
  const objs = await rpc({ command: "account_objects", account: addr, ledger_index: "validated", type: "mptoken" });
  return (objs.result.account_objects ?? []).find((o: any) => o.MPTokenIssuanceID === state.issuanceId);
}

let a = await mptOf(holder.address);
if (!a) die(`${holder.address} holds no MPToken for ${state.issuanceId}`);

// A freshly-merged or reset balance is the canonical EncZero, which CLAIMS.md
// F-1 records as PUBLICLY known to be zero. Merge the inbox if that is where we
// are, so there is something to send.
const [encZero] = await tool("enczero", state.holderElGamal.pk, accountIdHex(holder.address), state.issuanceId);
if (!a.ConfidentialBalanceSpending || a.ConfidentialBalanceSpending === encZero) {
  console.log("spending balance is the canonical EncZero — merging the inbox first");
  const r = await submit({ TransactionType: "ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox", MPTokenIssuanceID: state.issuanceId }, holder.seed);
  if (!r.engine.startsWith("tes")) die(`merge failed: ${r.engine}`);
  a = await mptOf(holder.address);
}

// Read for THIS SCRIPT's own preconditions only — so it can fail early with a
// sentence instead of watching the signer refuse. The signer re-reads every one
// of these itself and builds against its own read, not against these values.
const balance = Number((await tool("decrypt", a.ConfidentialBalanceSpending, state.holderElGamal.sk, "0", "5000"))[0]);
const b = await mptOf(holderB.address);
if (!b?.HolderEncryptionKey) die(`${holderB.address} has no registered HolderEncryptionKey`);
if (balance < AMOUNT) die(`balance ${balance} is below the amount ${AMOUNT}`);

console.log(`\nthis script's preconditions (the signer reads its own copy of all of it):`);
console.log(`  holder        ${holder.address}`);
console.log(`  balance       ${balance}`);
console.log(`  destination   ${holderB.address}`);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 2. The holder profile — **secrets and policy, nothing else.**
//    ⚠ It carries the seed; see the header.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
rmSync(WORK, { recursive: true, force: true });
mkdirSync(WORK, { recursive: true });
// ⚠ **Secrets and policy only.** Every ledger value that used to be here is
// read by the signer. Putting one back would not be ignored — the profile
// refuses it by name, because a signer that silently preferred a stale local
// value to the ledger is the gap step 2 closed, reopened by a config file.
const profile = {
  account_seed: holder.seed,
  elgamal_sk: state.holderElGamal.sk,
  elgamal_pk: state.holderElGamal.pk,
  issuance_id: state.issuanceId,
  fee_drops: 5000,
  network_id: 2,
  ledger_endpoint: "https://s.devnet.rippletest.net:51234/",
  amount_search_to: 5000,
};
writeFileSync(`${WORK}/profile.json`, JSON.stringify(profile, null, 2));

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 3. Start the signer and talk to it over the Unix socket.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
const child = spawn(SIGNER, [], {
  env: {
    ...process.env,
    WCONF_SIGNER_PROFILE: `${WORK}/profile.json`,
    WCONF_SIGNER_SOCKET: SOCKET,
    WCONF_SIGNER_STORE: `${WORK}/randomness`,
  },
  stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"],
});
child.stdout.on("data", (d) => process.stdout.write(`  [signer] ${d}`));
child.stderr.on("data", (d) => process.stderr.write(`  [signer] ${d}`));

# Session 5 spike — wiring the prover into the signer

**Architecture §6 step 3.** Everything cryptographic here is done by
`signer/`; these files read public ledger state, hand the signer a profile,
drive it over a Unix socket, and submit what it returns. **Nothing in this
directory signs, proves, or holds a proof.**

**Throwaway harness code. Not library code. Do not build on it.** Committed for
the reason `tools/spike-2026-08-17/` and `tools/spike-2026-08-18/` are: under
standing prohibition **P-8**, a value whose generator is unavailable is not
checkable. `xrpl-vectors.json` is the clearest case — it is the evidence
`signer/tests/xrpl_vectors.rs` checks against, and it would be worthless without
the script beside it.

**Devnet only.** Both drivers route through the 2026-08-17 spike's `convert.ts`,
which refuses any `network_id` but 2. **The signer refuses it independently**,
in its own reader, before it reads anything else.

## ⚠ Updated 2026-08-19 — the profile these drivers write is much smaller

Architecture §6 step 2 is built. The drivers no longer read the sequence number,
the balance, the balance ciphertext, `ConfidentialBalanceVersion`, the
registration state, the issuer key, the auditor key, the last-ledger bound or
the destination's `HolderEncryptionKey` and write them into a profile. **The
signer reads every one of them itself**, and a profile that still carries one
**fails to load, by name** — which is how the half-updated version of these
files was caught.

`devnet-clean-account.ts` shows the change most clearly: its two Sends used to
need the balance and version re-read and re-injected between them, because the
first Send moved both. They now take `{}`.

## What each file is

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `xrpl-vectors.ts` | **The generator.** Produces `xrpl-vectors.json` from `ripple-binary-codec@2.9.0`, `ripple-keypairs@2.0.0` and `ripple-address-codec@5.0.1` — three implementations this project did not write. Run bare to **check for drift**; `--write` regenerates |
| `xrpl-vectors.json` | 8 keys (secp256k1 **and** ed25519), 21 field definitions, 4 signed transactions, 7 VL-prefix boundaries. `signer/tests/xrpl_vectors.rs` fails if the Rust encoder disagrees with any of it |
| `devnet-signer-send.ts` | **The objective.** A `ConfidentialMPTSend` built, proved and signed by `signer/`, then submitted. Sends a deliberately false `claimed` block, so the confirmation's honesty is exercised on the real path |
| `devnet-clean-account.ts` | Builds a holder whose **every** confidential transaction comes from `signer/`, so architecture §6 step 4's falsifier can be fired against our own work rather than against a contaminated history |

## Capturing upstream feedback

This project produces a second output alongside the artifact: observations for the RippleX teams working on privacy and confidentiality. Capture is a coding-session job because friction is only visible at the moment you hit it — an error code that does not say which proof failed, a field the docs describe wrongly, a build step nothing warns you about. By the next session it reads as normal and you stop noticing.

When you hit one, add a row to `UPSTREAM-FEEDBACK.md` under `Observed`, with what you were doing and what you expected. Do not grade it, do not write it up, do not decide whether it is worth sending. Capture and move on.

**Two slash commands carry the procedure**, because this is a repeated task and not a project convention: **`/upstream-issue`** drafts a filing from a finding, **`/issue-review`** attacks the draft before it is sent. ⚠ **User-invoked, in `.claude/commands/` beside the other three** — never model-invoked, because filing needs the owner's authorisation every time. ⚠ **Run `/issue-review` before every filing** — protocol rule 1 gates on it.

⚠ **The first thing either skill does is read the TARGET repository's own issue template**, and that is not a formality. **Measured 2026-09-01: `XRPLF/rippled` sets `blank_issues_enabled: false` and offers only `bug_report.md` and `feature_request.md`.** `rippled#8118` fit neither, was filed anyway, and was **closed without comment**. The other three XRPLF repositories have no templates. ⚠ **Re-check rather than inheriting that sentence.**

⚠ **FILING is governed by `docs/UPSTREAM-FILING-PROTOCOL.md`, ruled 2026-09-01, and `make check-filing` enforces the mechanical half.** Five rules: an adversarial review runs **BEFORE** filing and gates it; a prose word cap **the gate prints** with one concrete ask; **no positives-only filings to a bug tracker**; no negative claim without its recorded search; plain English and short sentences. ⚠ **The 2026-09-01 audit found every claim in the six open filings still standing at upstream HEAD — so the research was sound and the ORDER OF OPERATIONS was the defect.** A review that runs after submission cannot prevent anything; it can only produce a public correction.

Two rules that apply to capture:

- **Positive observations count**, but only when specific and non-obvious — a design decision that turns out to be better than it looks once you have read the source. Anything that could be said about any competent codebase is padding.
- **Nothing moves out of `Observed` in a coding session.** Promotion requires verification against source, a grade, and a citation, and sending is a Desktop-project decision. A coding session that files an upstream issue on its own initiative has skipped the review this project applies to everything else.

## Branches

`<kind>/<slug>`, and the kinds are this project's own vocabulary rather than the
generic `feat`/`fix` set: **`build/`** for an architecture §6 step, **`review/`**
for a rotation, **`spike/`** for a throwaway, **`decision/`** for an ADR or a
ruling, **`research/`** for a TASK ZERO question, **`tools/`** for harnesses.
`build/step-3-wire-the-prover` is the model.

⚠ **This convention was followed for the first six branches and then dropped for
six in a row** — `step2-ledger-read`, `step6-keygen-onboarding`, `adr-0002-rev4`,
`rulings-b14-b15-adr0002`, `close-out-session`, `step7-convert-back-and-e76`.
Nobody noticed until 2026-08-25, because nothing wrote it down. It is written
down here now, which is the only reason a seventh will not drift the same way.

built 2026-09-09. `make break-emphasis-gate` is the mutations that verify it and
`make break-emphasis-gate-self-test` verifies those.

From `transactions.macro` and `sfields.macro` at 3.3.0, cross-checked against the spec. Type numbers match exactly.

| Tx | Type | Delegable | ZKProof | Proof obligation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ConfidentialMPTConvert` | 85 | **No** | 64 B, optional | Schnorr PoK, only when registering the holder key. Otherwise the disclosed `BlindingFactor` lets validators verify deterministically with no ZKP. |
| `ConfidentialMPTMergeInbox` | 86 | Yes | none | Proof-free. Value is known to ledger state. |
| `ConfidentialMPTConvertBack` | 87 | Yes | 816 B | 128 B sigma (balance ownership, key linkage) + 688 B single Bulletproof |
| `ConfidentialMPTSend` | 88 | Yes | **946 B**, fixed | 192 B sigma (ciphertext consistency across sender/receiver/issuer/auditor, amount linkage, balance linkage) + 754 B aggregated Bulletproof over two 64-bit values |
| `ConfidentialMPTClawback` | 89 | Yes | 64 B | Sigma proof that `sfIssuerEncryptedBalance` encrypts the stated plaintext |

**~~Byte values are Grade B pending GAP-6.~~ Grade A as of 2026-08-16.** `Protocol.h:466–471` verifies the *structure* — `kEcSendProofLength = kEcSendSigmaProofLength + kEcDoubleBulletproofLength`, enforced at preflight. The macros it resolves to are now read at mpt-crypto `0.4.0-rc4`: `SECP256K1_COMPACT_STANDARD_PROOF_SIZE 192`, `kMPT_DOUBLE_BULLETPROOF_SIZE 754`, `kMPT_SINGLE_BULLETPROOF_SIZE 688`, `SECP256K1_COMPACT_CONVERTBACK_PROOF_SIZE 128`, `SECP256K1_COMPACT_CLAWBACK_PROOF_SIZE 64`, `kMPT_SCHNORR_PROOF_SIZE 64`. Every value in the table above is confirmed. The header additionally derives each sigma size from its scalar count — send is (e, z_m, z_r, z_b, z_rho, z_sk) ∈ Z_q⁶ = 192 B — so the numbers are internally cross-checked as well.

FINDINGS — most severe first

1. [P1] Limit the zero-knowledge explanation to transactions that prove — web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:41–43
HIGH — “So each confidential transaction carries zero-knowledge proofs, which every validator checks without learning the amount.” TASK ZERO §3 explicitly makes MergeInbox proof-free and later Converts proof-free; Convert and ConvertBack also publish their amounts. This additionally contradicts the README’s Proofs table and this page’s public-boundary panels. Replace the universal statement with a Send-specific explanation, distinguishing proof-free operations and public conversion amounts.

2. [P1] State the assumptions behind the corrected arithmetic example — CLAIMS.md:510–510
HIGH — R-7’s replacement, “The other 100 is either still held or has left by confidential transfer.”, is not exhaustive under E-12/E-21: start at zero, Convert and merge 500, ConvertBack 400, then claw back the remaining 100 on a clawback-enabled issuance. Nothing remains held or transferred. The amount can also be divided between retention and Sends rather than taking one whole-100 alternative. Qualify the example with a zero opening balance and no clawback, and describe the remaining 100 as split between holdings and Sends; carry that wording into the changed explainer and hosted page. The burn mechanism is recorded in [CLAIMS.md:53](CLAIMS.md#L53).

3. [P1] Keep the new disclaimer compatible with the wording test — web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:215–216
MEDIUM — “It is not audited, not production-ready and not safe to put value behind.” is correctly negative under P-5, but its source line containing `production-ready` lacks the exemption required by `web/api/disclosure.test.ts:128–132`. Running `bun test web/api web/hosted` produces 191 passes and this one failure at line 135. Keep the disclaimer and either add its P-5 citation on the scanned line or update the detector to recognise the negation; do not remove the warning to make the test pass.

4. [P2] Preserve the seed-rederivation exception in the key-loss limit — web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:202–204
MEDIUM — “If a holder loses it, the balance cannot be spent, and the only remedy is an issuer clawback, which destroys the balance.” drops the exception demonstrated by E-119 and retained in the README and capability matrix: a holder retaining the master seed can reconstruct a derived ElGamal key. P-10 prohibits protocol recovery, not this application-level reconstruction; [CLAUDE.md:127](CLAUDE.md#L127) explicitly requires keeping those layers separate. Say “irretrievably loses it, including any seed from which it can be re-derived” and retain the seed-rederivation qualification.

5. [P2] Disclose that this project enables the clawback power — web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:208–209
MEDIUM — “If the token allows clawback, the issuer can destroy a holder’s whole confidential balance.” states E-21’s protocol condition but omits that this project sets the flag. E-223 records both live issuances with `Flags=224`, and `facility/run-facility.ts` sets `tfMPTCanClawback`; the README explicitly says the issuer can therefore burn a balance in every demonstration here. Preserve that application of the condition instead of leaving readers to guess whether the example or displayed token permits it. Add “This project’s demonstrations enable it” and cite E-223.

6. [P2] Enforce citation pinning beyond raw HTML strings — tools/check-web-hosted.ts:383–386
MEDIUM — The new invariant, “A link into the repository at any commit but the build's would cite text the gate never saw.”, is not enforced for all admitted citations. codex
The explainer makes a false universal proof claim and omits important recovery, transaction-flow and facility-run qualifications. The new citation gate accepts wrong-commit links in encoded HTML and JavaScript, and the targeted tests fail on the new disclaimer.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Limit the zero-knowledge explanation to transactions that prove — $USER_TMP/T/r060a.qD7Xey/repo/web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:41-43
  HIGH — “So each confidential transaction carries zero-knowledge proofs, which every validator checks without learning the amount.” TASK ZERO §3 explicitly makes MergeInbox proof-free and later Converts proof-free; Convert and ConvertBack also publish their amounts. This contradicts the README’s Proofs table and this page’s public-boundary panels. Replace the universal statement with a Send-specific explanation, distinguishing proof-free operations and public conversion amounts.

- [P1] Keep the new disclaimer compatible with the wording test — $USER_TMP/T/r060a.qD7Xey/repo/web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:215-216
  MEDIUM — “It is not audited, not production-ready and not safe to put value behind.” is correctly negative under P-5, but its source line containing `production-ready` lacks the exemption required by `web/api/disclosure.test.ts:128–132`. Running `bun test web/api web/hosted` produces 191 passes and this one failure. Keep the disclaimer and either add its P-5 citation on the scanned line or update the detector to recognise the negation.

- [P2] Preserve the seed-rederivation exception in the key-loss limit — $USER_TMP/T/r060a.qD7Xey/repo/web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:202-204
  MEDIUM — “If a holder loses it, the balance cannot be spent, and the only remedy is an issuer clawback, which destroys the balance.” drops the exception demonstrated by E-119 and retained in the README and capability matrix: a holder retaining the master seed can reconstruct a derived ElGamal key. P-10 prohibits protocol recovery, not application-level reconstruction; [CLAUDE.md:127](CLAUDE.md#L127) explicitly requires keeping those layers separate. Qualify this as irretrievable loss, including loss of any seed from which the key can be re-derived.

- [P2] Disclose that this project enables the clawback power — $USER_TMP/T/r060a.qD7Xey/repo/web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:208-209
  MEDIUM — “If the token allows clawback, the issuer can destroy a holder’s whole confidential balance.” states E-21’s condition but omits that this project sets the flag. E-223 records both live issuances with `Flags=224`, and `facility/run-facility.ts` sets `tfMPTCanClawback`; the README explicitly applies the power to every demonstration here. Add that these demonstrations enable clawback rather than leaving readers to guess whether the condition applies. The project-specific disclosure is recorded in [CLAIMS.md:283](CLAIMS.md#L283).

- [P2] Enforce citation pinning beyond raw HTML strings — $USER_TMP/T/r060a.qD7Xey/repo/tools/check-web-hosted.ts:383-386
  MEDIUM — The new invariant, “A link into the repository at any commit but the build's would cite text the gate never saw.”, is not enforced for all admitted citations. On copies of the supplied build, `runChecks()` returns no findings for a wrong-commit blob URL placed literally or assembled in a loaded JavaScript asset. It also accepts an HTML href using `https&#58;` and `blob&#47;` before a different 40-hex commit: check 5 decodes and admits it, while this raw-HTML regex misses it. Apply the expected-commit constraint to canonicalised citation URLs across HTML and bundled code, with controls for both bypasses.

- [P2] Carry the facility run’s remote-source qualification — $USER_TMP/T/r060a.qD7Xey/repo/web/app/src/hosted/routes/how-it-works.tsx:145-145
  MEDIUM — “This project built that facility on XLS-96 and ran it on Devnet, in 28 validated transactions:” omits the condition E-146 and B-18 preserve. The walkthrough explicitly says this qualification must travel with the run claim: it used a remote ledger source under E-151’s risk acceptance, not B-15’s loopback conditions, and establishes acceptance and balance agreement rather than the loopback obligation. Add that qualification and E-151/B-18 to the panel’s sources; see [FACILITY-WALKTHROUGH:11–15](docs/explainer/FACILITY-WALKTHROUGH-2026-08-20.md#L11-L15).

  MEDIUM — “Moves tokens from the holder’s public balance into confidential form.” leaves out the condition needed to follow this Convert → Send lifecycle. The page mentions merging only for the recipient of a Send, omitting the distinction that previously broke the facility’s balance model.
